bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: =【陳紀九】=

translations.literal: 【Chen Records 9】
translations.idiomatic: 【Chen Records 9】

sentences.zh: 起重光赤奮若，盡昭陽單閼，凡三年。

translations.literal: Beginning with Chongguang Chifenruo, ending with Zhaoyang Danqian, altogether three years.
translations.idiomatic: This annal spans from the year Chongguang Chifenruo through Zhaoyang Danqian, covering three years in all.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，壬午，以晉安王伯恭為尚書左僕射，吏部尚書袁憲為右僕射。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, on the day Renwu, the Prince of Jin'an, Bo Gong, was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Yuan Xian, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the renwu day of the first month, Prince Jin'an Bo Gong was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Yuan Xian, Minister of Personnel, was appointed Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 憲，樞之弟也。

translations.literal: Xian was the younger brother of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian was the younger brother of Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 2周改元大定。

translations.literal: 2 The Zhou changed the era name to Dading.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Zhou court changed the era name to Dading.

sentences.zh: 3二月，甲寅，隋王始受相國、百揆、九錫之命，建台置官。

translations.literal: 3 In the second month, on the day Jiayin, the Prince of Sui first received the commission of Chancellor of State, overseer of all affairs, and the Nine Bestowals, and established a headquarters with officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiayin, Prince Sui Yang Jian first accepted appointment as Chancellor of State with authority over all government and the Nine Bestowals, and set up a chancellery with its own staff.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，詔進王妃獨孤氏為王后，世子勇為太子。

translations.literal: On the day Bingchen, an edict advanced the prince's consort, the Lady Dugu, to queen, and the heir Yong to crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen an edict elevated Lady Dugu, the prince's wife, to queen and named the heir Yang Yong crown prince.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同大將軍庾季才，勸隋王宜以今月甲子應天受命。

translations.literal: The General of the Palace Gate with the Honorary Title Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, Yu Jicai, urged the Prince of Sui that on the day Jiazi of this month he should receive Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jicai, a general with the honorary rank Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, urged Prince Sui to take the throne on the jiazi day of that month as Heaven's chosen ruler.

sentences.zh: 太傅李穆、開府儀同大將軍盧賁亦勸之。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor Li Mu and the General Lu Ben with the same honorary rank also urged him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Li Mu and General Lu Ben likewise pressed him to accept.

sentences.zh: 於是周主下詔，遜居別宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Zhou sovereign issued an edict and withdrew to a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor then issued an edict abdicating and retired to a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 甲子，命兼太傅□巳公椿奉冊，大宗伯趙煚奉皇帝璽紱，禪位於隋。

translations.literal: On the day Jiazi, he ordered the Concurrent Grand Tutor, Duke of Qi Chun, to present the abdication document, and the Grand Director of Ceremonies Zhao Jiong to present the imperial seal and ribbon, and abdicated the throne to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he had Concurrent Grand Tutor Duke of Qi Chun deliver the abdication text and Grand Director of Ceremonies Zhao Jiong present the imperial seal and cord, ceding the throne to Yang Jian of Sui.

sentences.zh: 隋主冠遠遊冠；

translations.literal: The Sui ruler put on the Far Roaming cap;
translations.idiomatic: The new Sui ruler first donned the Far Roaming cap;

sentences.zh: 受冊、璽，改服紗帽、黃袍；

translations.literal: received the document and seal, and changed to a gauze cap and yellow robe;
translations.idiomatic: received the register and seal, then changed into a gauze cap and yellow robe;

sentences.zh: 入御臨光殿，服袞冕，如元會之儀。

translations.literal: entered and took the throne in the Hall of Approaching Light, donned the dragon robes and coronet, and performed the rites as at the New Year's audience.
translations.idiomatic: entered the Hall of Approaching Light, assumed full imperial regalia, and held court with the ceremony of the New Year's audience.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元開皇。

translations.literal: He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Kaihuang.
translations.idiomatic: He declared a general amnesty and proclaimed the Kaihuang era.

sentences.zh: 命有司奉冊祀於南郊。

translations.literal: He ordered the officials to offer the document in sacrifice at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the relevant offices to report the accession to Heaven with rites at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 遣少塚宰元孝矩代太子勇鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: He sent the Junior Director of the Imperial Clan Yuan Xiaoju to replace Crown Prince Yong in garrisoning Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Junior Director of the Imperial Clan Yuan Xiaoju to Luoyang to relieve Crown Prince Yong of duty there.

sentences.zh: 孝矩名矩，以字行，天賜之孫也；

translations.literal: Xiaoju's given name was Ju, but he was known by his style name; he was a grandson of Tiansi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoju was formally named Ju but was known by his style; he was a grandson of the Northern Wei prince Tiansi.

sentences.zh: 女為太子妃。

translations.literal: His daughter was the crown prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was married to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 少內史崔仲方勸隋主除周六官，依漢、魏之舊，從之。

translations.literal: The Junior Palace Scribe Cui Zhongfang urged the Sui ruler to abolish the Zhou six ministries and follow the old systems of Han and Wei; he agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Palace Scribe Cui Zhongfang urged the emperor to abolish the Northern Zhou six-ministry system and restore Han- and Wei-style government, and he agreed.

sentences.zh: 置三師、三公及尚書、門下、內史、秘書、內侍五省，御史、都水二台，太常等十一寺，左右衛等十二府，以分司統職。

translations.literal: He established the Three Preceptors, the Three Excellencies, and the five departments of the Masters of Writing, the Chancellery, the Palace Secretariat, the Secretariat, and the Palace Attendants, the two bureaus of the Censorate and the Directorate of Waterways, the eleven directorates such as the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and the twelve guards such as the Left and Right Guards, to divide duties and govern offices.
translations.idiomatic: He set up the Three Preceptors and Three Excellencies, five central departments (Masters of Writing, Chancellery, Palace Secretariat, Secretariat, and Palace Attendants), the Censorate and Directorate of Waterways, eleven court directorates including the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and twelve guard offices including the Left and Right Guards, dividing responsibilities among them.

sentences.zh: 又置上柱國至都督十一等勳官，以酬勤勞；

translations.literal: He also established eleven grades of merit offices from Upper Pillar of State down to Commander, to reward diligent service;
translations.idiomatic: He also created eleven grades of merit titles from Upper Pillar of State down to Commander to reward military service;

sentences.zh: 特進至朝散大夫七等散官，以加文武官之有德聲者。

translations.literal: and seven grades of honorary offices from Special Advancement down to Grand Master for Court Discussion, to honor civil and military officials of established virtue and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: and seven grades of honorary posts from Special Advancement to Grand Master for Court Discussion for civil and military officials of proven merit and reputation.

sentences.zh: 改侍中為納言。

translations.literal: He changed the title Attendant-in-Ordinary to Supplicator.
translations.idiomatic: The title Attendant-in-Ordinary was renamed Supplicator.

sentences.zh: 以相國司馬高熲為尚書左僕射，兼納言，相國司錄京兆虞慶則為內史監，兼吏部尚書，相國內郎李德林為內史令。

translations.literal: He made the Chancellor of State's Major Gao Jiong Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent Supplicator, the Chancellor's Recorder Yu Qingze of Jingzhao Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrent Minister of Personnel, and the Chancellor's Palace Gentleman Li Delin Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong, the chancellor's chief administrator, became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent Supplicator; Yu Qingze of Jingzhao, the chancellor's recorder, became Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrent Minister of Personnel; and Li Delin, a palace gentleman on the chancellor's staff, became Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，追尊皇考為武元皇帝，廟號太祖；

translations.literal: On the day Yichou, he posthumously honored his late father as Emperor Wuyuan, with the temple name Taizu;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou he posthumously honored his father as Emperor Wuyuan, temple name Taizu;

sentences.zh: 皇妣呂氏為元明皇后。

translations.literal: and his late mother, the Lady Lü, as Empress Yuanming.
translations.idiomatic: and his mother, Lady Lü, as Empress Yuanming.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，修廟社。

translations.literal: On the day Bingyin, he restored the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin he restored the imperial ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 立王后獨孤為皇后，王太子勇為皇太子。

translations.literal: He installed the queen, Lady Dugu, as empress, and the prince's heir Yong as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He formally enthroned Lady Dugu as empress and Yang Yong as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以大將軍趙煚為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day Dingmao, he made the General Zhao Jiong Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he appointed General Zhao Jiong Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 己巳，封周靜帝為介公。

translations.literal: On the day Jisi, he enfeoffed the Zhou Emperor Jing as Duke of Jie.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he ennobled the deposed Zhou Emperor Jing as Duke of Jie.

sentences.zh: 周氏諸王皆降爵為公。

translations.literal: All the princes of the Zhou house were reduced in rank to dukes.
translations.idiomatic: All princes of the Zhou imperial clan were demoted to the rank of duke.

sentences.zh: 初，劉、鄭矯詔以隋主輔政，楊后雖不預謀，然以嗣子幼沖，恐權在他族，聞之，甚喜。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu and Zheng had forged an edict appointing the Prince of Sui as regent. Although Empress Yang had not taken part in the plot, because the heir was young and she feared power would pass to another clan, when she heard of it she was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Fang and Zheng Yi had forged an edict making Prince Sui regent. Empress Yang had not been in on the plot, but with the heir still a child she feared another clan would seize power, and she was delighted when she heard the news.

sentences.zh: 後知其父有異圖，意頗不平，形於言色，及禪位，憤惋逾甚。

translations.literal: Later, when she learned her father harbored designs of his own, she was quite resentful, and it showed in her words and expression; when the abdication took place, her anger and grief grew still worse.
translations.idiomatic: When she later realized her father intended to take the throne himself, she grew deeply resentful, and her feelings showed plainly; at the abdication her outrage only deepened.

sentences.zh: 隋主內甚愧之，改封樂平公主，久之，欲奪其志。

translations.literal: The Sui ruler felt deeply ashamed toward her within, enfeoffed her as Princess of Leping, and after a long while wished to change her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor was inwardly ashamed toward her, created her Princess of Leping, and after some time tried to persuade her to remarry.

sentences.zh: 公主誓不許，乃止。

translations.literal: The princess swore she would not consent, and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The princess vowed she would never agree, and he gave up the idea.

sentences.zh: 隋主與周載下大夫北平榮建緒有舊，隋主將受禪，建緒為息州刺史。

translations.literal: The Sui ruler had an old friendship with Rong Jianxu of Beiping, a Lower Grand Master under the Zhou; when the Sui ruler was about to receive the abdication, Jianxu was governor of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had been friends with Rong Jianxu of Beiping, a Zhou lower grand master; when Yang Jian was about to take the throne, Rong was serving as governor of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 將之官，隋主謂曰：「且躊躇，當共取富貴。

translations.literal: As he was about to take up his post, the Sui ruler said to him, "Wait a while—we shall share wealth and honor together.
translations.idiomatic: As Rong was leaving to take up his post, Yang Jian told him, "Hold off a little—we will rise to wealth and rank together.

sentences.zh: 」建緒正色曰：「明公此旨，非僕所聞。

translations.literal: " Jianxu said sternly, "Your Excellency's words are not something I care to hear.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong replied gravely, "My lord, that is not language I wish to hear from you.

sentences.zh: 」及即位，來朝，帝謂之曰：「卿亦悔不？

translations.literal: " After he took the throne, Jianxu came to court, and the emperor said to him, "Do you regret it now?
translations.idiomatic: " After the enthronement Rong came to court, and the emperor asked, "Do you regret it now?

sentences.zh: 」建緒稽首曰：「臣位非徐廣，情類楊彪。

translations.literal: " Jianxu bowed his head and said, "Your servant is not in Xu Guang's position, but my feelings are like Yang Biao's.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong kowtowed and said, "I am no Xu Guang in rank, but my loyalty is that of Yang Biao.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「朕雖不曉書語，亦知卿此言不遜！

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed and said, "Though I am no scholar of written lore, I know your words are impertinent!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed and said, "I may not be a man of letters, but I know an insult when I hear one!

sentences.zh: 上柱國竇毅之女，聞隋受禪，自投堂下，撫膺太息曰：「恨我不為男子，救舅氏之患！

translations.literal: The daughter of the Upper Pillar of State Dou Yi, when she heard that Sui had received the abdication, threw herself down in the hall, beat her breast, and sighed deeply, saying, "I regret I am not a man, to save my mother's clan from disaster!
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Yi's daughter heard that Yang Jian had taken the throne, she threw herself to the floor, clutched her breast, and cried, "If only I were a man, that I might save my uncle's house from ruin!

sentences.zh: 」毅及襄陽公主掩其口曰；

translations.literal: " Yi and the Princess of Xiangyang covered her mouth and said:
translations.idiomatic: " Dou Yi and the Princess of Xiangyang clapped a hand over her mouth and said:

sentences.zh: 「汝勿妄言，滅吾族！

translations.literal: "Do not speak rashly—you will destroy our clan!
translations.idiomatic: "Do not talk like that—you will bring ruin on our whole family!

sentences.zh: 」毅由是奇之。

translations.literal: " From this Yi regarded her as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: " From that moment Dou Yi regarded her as remarkable.

sentences.zh: 及長，以適唐公李淵。

translations.literal: When she grew up, she was given in marriage to Li Yuan, Duke of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age she was married to Li Yuan, Duke of Tang.

sentences.zh: 淵，昺之子也。

translations.literal: Yuan was a son of Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan was a son of Li Bing.

sentences.zh: 虞慶則勸隋主盡滅宇文氏，高熲、楊惠亦依違從之。

translations.literal: Yu Qingze urged the Sui ruler to exterminate the Yuwen clan entirely; Gao Jiong and Yang Hui also vacillated and went along.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qingze urged the emperor to wipe out the entire Yuwen clan; Gao Jiong and Yang Hui wavered but eventually agreed.

sentences.zh: 李德林固爭，以為不可。

translations.literal: Li Delin argued firmly that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Li Delin argued strenuously that this must not be done.

sentences.zh: 隋主作色曰：「君書生，不足與議此！

translations.literal: The Sui ruler changed color and said, "You are a bookish man—not fit to discuss this!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened. "You are a scholar," he said, "unfit to discuss such matters!

sentences.zh: 」於是周太祖孫譙公乾惲、冀公絢，閔帝子紀公湜，明帝子酆公貞、宋公實，高祖子漢公贊、秦公贄、曹公允、道公充、蔡公兌、荊公元，宣帝子萊公衍、郢公術皆死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Zhou Grand Ancestor's grandsons, the Dukes of Qiao Gan Yun and Ji Xuan, the Min Emperor's son the Duke of Ji Shi, the Ming Emperor's sons the Dukes of Feng Zhen and Song Shi, the High Emperor's sons the Dukes of Han Zan, Qin Zan, Cao Yun, Dao Chong, Cai Dui, and Jing Yuan, and the Xuan Emperor's sons the Dukes of Lai Yan and Ying Shu, all died.
translations.idiomatic: " In the purge that followed, the Yuwen princes were killed: among them Gan Yun and Xuan of Qiao and Ji, grandsons of the Zhou founder; Shi of Ji, son of Emperor Min; Zhen of Feng and Shi of Song, sons of Emperor Ming; Zan of Han, Zan of Qin, Yun of Cao, Chong of Dao, Dui of Cai, and Yuan of Jing, sons of Emperor Gaozu; and Yan of Lai and Shu of Ying, sons of Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 德林由是品位不進。

translations.literal: From this Delin's rank advanced no further.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Li Delin's career stalled.

sentences.zh: 4乙亥，上耕藉田。

translations.literal: 4 On the day Yihai, the emperor plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the emperor performed the ceremonial spring plowing in the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 5隋主封其弟邵公慧為滕王，安公爽為衛王，子雁門公廣為晉王，俊為秦王，秀為越王，諒為漢王。

translations.literal: 5 The Sui ruler enfeoffed his younger brother the Duke of Shao, Hui, as Prince of Teng; the Duke of An, Shuang, as Prince of Wei; his son the Duke of Yanmen, Guang, as Prince of Jin; Jun as Prince of Qin; Xiu as Prince of Yue; and Liang as Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enfeoffed his brother Hui, Duke of Shao, as Prince of Teng; his brother Shuang, Duke of An, as Prince of Wei; and his sons Guang of Yanmen as Prince of Jin, Jun as Prince of Qin, Xiu as Prince of Yue, and Liang as Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 隋主賜李穆詔曰：「公既舊德，且又父黨。

translations.literal: The Sui ruler sent Li Mu an edict saying, "You are a man of long-standing merit, and moreover of my father's generation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Li Mu an edict: "You are a man of long service and of my father's generation.

sentences.zh: 敬惠來旨，義無有違。

translations.literal: I respectfully received your gracious message; in duty there is no refusing.
translations.idiomatic: I have received your gracious word with respect and cannot in conscience refuse.

sentences.zh: 即以今月十三日恭膺天命。

translations.literal: I shall therefore reverently accept Heaven's mandate on the thirteenth of this month.
translations.idiomatic: I shall therefore take the throne on the thirteenth of this month as Heaven commands.

sentences.zh: 」俄而穆入朝，帝以穆為太師，贊拜不名；

translations.literal: " Soon afterward Mu came to court, and the emperor made Mu Grand Preceptor, with the privilege of being addressed without his name in memorials;
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Li Mu came to court and was appointed Grand Preceptor, with the privilege that memorials need not name him;

sentences.zh: 子孫雖在襁褓，悉拜儀同，一門執象笏者百餘人，貴盛無比。

translations.literal: even his descendants still in swaddling clothes were all appointed to the rank Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, and more than a hundred in the household held ivory tablets—wealth and glory without parallel.
translations.idiomatic: even infants in the family were given the rank Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, and more than a hundred Li clansmen held court tablets—honor unmatched in the realm.

sentences.zh: 又以上柱國竇熾為太傅，幽州總管於翼為太尉。

translations.literal: He also made the Upper Pillar of State Dou Chi Grand Tutor and Yu Yi, regional commander of Youzhou, Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Dou Chi Grand Tutor and Yu Yi, commander of Youzhou, Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 李穆上表乞骸骨，詔曰：「呂尚以期頤佐周，張蒼以華皓相漢，高才命世，不拘常禮。

translations.literal: Li Mu submitted a memorial asking to retire; the edict said, "Lü Shang aided Zhou at the age of a centenarian, and Zhang Cang served Han in his white-haired years—men of transcendent talent are not bound by ordinary ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mu asked to retire, the edict replied, "Lü Shang aided the Zhou past the age of ninety, and Zhang Cang served Han in his white-haired old age—men of rare ability are not bound by ordinary rules.

sentences.zh: 」仍以穆年耆，敕蠲朝集，有大事，就第詢訪。

translations.literal: " Because Mu was aged, he was excused from court assemblies; on great affairs, inquiry would be made at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: " Because of Li Mu's great age he was excused from regular court attendance; on important matters the emperor would consult him at home.

sentences.zh: 美陽公蘇威，綽之子也，少有令名，周晉公護強以女妻之。

translations.literal: Su Wei, Duke of Meiyang, was a son of Su Chuo; in youth he had a fine reputation. The Zhou Duke of Jin, Hu, forced his daughter on him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Duke of Meiyang, was the son of Su Chuo and had been celebrated from youth. The Zhou regent Yuwen Hu compelled him to marry his daughter.

sentences.zh: 威見護專權，恐禍及己，屏居山寺，以諷讀為娛。

translations.literal: Wei saw that Hu monopolized power and feared disaster would reach him; he withdrew to live in a mountain temple, taking recitation of the Odes as his pastime.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Yuwen Hu's monopoly on power, Su Wei feared he would be implicated and withdrew to a mountain monastery, passing his days reciting the Odes.

sentences.zh: 周高祖聞其賢，除車騎大將軍、儀同三司，又除稍伯下大夫，皆辭疾不拜；

translations.literal: The Zhou High Emperor heard of his worth and appointed him General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, and later made him Lower Grand Master of Shaobo—all of which he declined on grounds of illness;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Zhou heard of his talent and offered him the posts of General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, and later Lower Grand Master of Shaobo—Su Wei declined each on grounds of illness;

sentences.zh: 宣帝就除開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: the Xuan Emperor then directly appointed him General of the Palace Gate with the Honorary Title Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan then simply appointed him General of the Palace Gate with the honorary rank Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 隋主為丞相，高熲薦之，隋主召見，與語，大悅；

translations.literal: When the Sui ruler was chancellor, Gao Jiong recommended him; the Sui ruler summoned him, spoke with him, and was greatly pleased;
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was chancellor, Gao Jiong recommended Su Wei; Yang summoned him, talked with him at length, and was delighted;

sentences.zh: 居月餘，聞將受禪，遁歸田裡。

translations.literal: after more than a month, hearing that the abdication was imminent, he fled back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: but after a month, hearing that the abdication was at hand, he slipped away to his home estate.

sentences.zh: 熲請追之，隋主曰：「此不欲預吾事耳，置之。

translations.literal: Jiong asked to pursue him; the Sui ruler said, "He does not wish to take part in my affairs—let him be.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong asked permission to bring him back; Yang Jian said, "He does not wish to be part of what I am doing—leave him alone.

sentences.zh: 」及受禪，征拜太子少保，追封其父為邳公，以威襲爵。

translations.literal: " After receiving the abdication, he was summoned and appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince; his father was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Pi, and Wei inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: " After the enthronement he was recalled and made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince; his father was posthumously created Duke of Pi, and Su Wei inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，隋以晉王廣為并州總管。

translations.literal: On the day Dingchou, Sui made Prince Jin Guang regional commander of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Prince Jin Yang Guang was appointed regional commander of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊子，以上開府儀同三司賀若弼為吳州總管，鎮廣陵；

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day Wuzi, he made He Ruo Bi, with the superior honorary rank Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, regional commander of Wuzhou, garrisoning Guangling;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuzi, He Ruo Bi was made regional commander of Wuzhou and stationed at Guangling;

sentences.zh: 和州刺史河南韓擒虎為廬州總管，鎮廬江。

translations.literal: and Han Qinhu of Henan, prefect of Hezhou, regional commander of Luzhou, garrisoning Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: and Han Qinhu of Henan, formerly prefect of Hezhou, regional commander of Luzhou, stationed at Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 隋主有併吞江南之志，問將帥於高熲，熲薦弼與擒虎，故置於南邊，使潛為經略。

translations.literal: The Sui ruler harbored the ambition to swallow the south of the Yangzi; he asked Gao Jiong about generals, and Jiong recommended Bi and Qinhu; therefore they were placed on the southern frontier to make secret preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor intended to conquer the south; he asked Gao Jiong for commanders, and Gao recommended He Ruo Bi and Han Qinhu. They were posted on the southern frontier to prepare the campaign in secret.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以太子少保蘇威兼納言、度支尚書。

translations.literal: On the day Wuxu, Su Wei, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, was made concurrent Supplicator and Minister of the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Su Wei was appointed concurrent Supplicator and Minister of Revenue while retaining his post as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 初，蘇綽在西魏，以國用不足，制徵稅法頗重，既而歎曰：「今所為者，譬如張弓，非平世法也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Su Chuo in Western Wei, because state revenue was insufficient, devised a tax law that was quite heavy; afterward he sighed and said, "What we are doing now is like drawing a bow taut—it is not the method of a peaceful age.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when state revenue ran short in Western Wei, Su Chuo had devised a heavy tax system. He later sighed, "What we have done is like drawing a bow to its limit—it is no policy for peaceful times.

sentences.zh: 後之君子，誰能弛之！

translations.literal: Which gentleman of later times will be able to relax it!
translations.idiomatic: What worthy man of later times will be able to loosen it!

sentences.zh: 」威聞其言，每以為己任。

translations.literal: " When Wei heard these words, he always took them as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: " Su Wei took those words as his personal mission.

sentences.zh: 至是，奏減賦役，務從輕簡，隋主悉從之，漸見親重，與高熲參掌朝政。

translations.literal: At this time he memorialized to reduce taxes and corvée labor, striving for lightness and simplicity; the Sui ruler followed him entirely, and he gradually came to be treated with intimacy and weight, sharing governance of court affairs with Gao Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Now he memorialized to cut taxes and labor service and simplify administration; the emperor approved everything, and Su Wei gradually became indispensable, sharing power with Gao Jiong.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗怒一人，將殺之；

translations.literal: The emperor once grew angry at a man and was about to execute him;
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor, enraged at a man, was about to have him executed;

sentences.zh: 威入邠進諫，帝不納，將自出斬之，威當帝前不去；

translations.literal: Wei entered and advanced with remonstrance; the emperor would not accept it and was about to go out himself to behead the man; Wei stood before the emperor and would not leave;
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei entered and remonstrated; the emperor refused to listen and started out to kill the man himself; Su Wei blocked his path and would not budge;

sentences.zh: 帝避之而出，威又遮止。

translations.literal: the emperor evaded him and went out, and Wei again blocked and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor tried to slip past him, but Su Wei blocked him again.

sentences.zh: 帝拂衣而入，良久，乃召威謝曰：「公能若是，吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: The emperor brushed his robes and went inside; after a long while he summoned Wei and apologized, saying, "If you can act thus, I have no worries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned away in anger, but after a long interval summoned Su Wei and said, "If you will act like this, I have nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 」賜馬二匹，錢十餘萬。

translations.literal: " He bestowed on him two horses and more than a hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: " He rewarded him with two horses and more than a hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 尋復兼大理卿、京兆尹、御史大夫，本官悉如故。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again made concurrent Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Governor of Jingzhao, and Censor-in-Chief, while his original posts all remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given concurrent appointments as Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Governor of the capital district, and Censor-in-Chief, while keeping his existing posts.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史安定梁毘，以威兼領五職，安繁戀劇，無舉賢自代之心，抗表劾威。

translations.literal: Liang Pi of Anding, Attending Secretary in the Censorate, because Wei concurrently held five offices, content with complexity and attached to heavy duties, with no mind to recommend the worthy to replace him, submitted a memorial impeaching Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Pi of Anding, an attending censor, impeached Su Wei on the grounds that holding five offices at once showed he clung to power and had no intention of recommending a successor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「蘇威朝夕孜孜，志存遠大，何遽迫之！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Su Wei is diligent morning and evening, his aims set on the far horizon—why press him so hastily!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Su Wei works tirelessly day and night with far-reaching aims—why hound him like this!

sentences.zh: 」因謂朝臣曰：「蘇威不值我，無以措其言；

translations.literal: " He then said to the court officials, "Were it not for me, Su Wei would have nowhere to set his words;
translations.idiomatic: " He told the court, "Without me, Su Wei would have no one to hear his counsel;

sentences.zh: 我不得蘇威，何以行其道。

translations.literal: without Su Wei, how could I carry out his Way?
translations.idiomatic: without Su Wei, how could I put his principles into practice?

sentences.zh: 楊素才辯無雙，至於斟酌古今，助我宣化，非威之匹也。

translations.literal: Yang Su's talent in debate is unmatched, and in weighing past and present to help me spread transformation he has no equal—but he is not Wei's match.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su is unrivaled in eloquence and in drawing on history to help me govern, but he is not Su Wei's equal.

sentences.zh: 威若逢亂世，南山四皓，豈易屈哉！

translations.literal: If Wei met a chaotic age, he would be like the Four Whiteheads of the Southern Mountains—how easily could he be bent!
translations.idiomatic: In troubled times Su Wei would be another of the Four Whiteheads of Mount Zhongnan—not a man easily bent to another's will!

sentences.zh: 」威嘗言於帝曰：「臣先人每戒臣云：『唯讀《孝經》一卷，足以立身治國，何用多為！

translations.literal: " Wei once said to the emperor, "My forebear always admonished me, saying, 'If you read only one scroll of the Classic of Filial Piety, it is enough to establish yourself and govern the state—what need for more!
translations.idiomatic: " Su Wei once told the emperor, "My father always warned me: 'One scroll of the Classic of Filial Piety is enough to live by and to govern with—why read more than you need?'

sentences.zh: 』」帝深然之。

translations.literal: '" The emperor deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: '" The emperor heartily agreed.

sentences.zh: 高熲深避權勢，上表遜位，讓於蘇威，帝欲成其美，聽解僕射。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong deeply shunned power; he submitted a memorial yielding his post and ceding it to Su Wei; the emperor wished to complete his fine act and allowed him to resign as Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong, wary of power, memorialized to step down in favor of Su Wei; the emperor, wishing to honor his generosity, accepted his resignation as Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 數日，帝曰：「蘇威高蹈前朝，熲能推舉。

translations.literal: After several days the emperor said, "Su Wei held himself aloof in the previous dynasty, and Jiong was able to recommend him.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the emperor said, "Su Wei stood apart under the Zhou, and Gao Jiong had the grace to recommend him.

sentences.zh: 吾聞進賢受上賞，寧可使之去官！

translations.literal: I have heard that advancing the worthy receives the highest reward—how could I let him leave office!
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that recommending the worthy deserves the highest reward—how can I let Gao Jiong leave office!

sentences.zh: 」命熲復位。

translations.literal: " He ordered Jiong restored to his post.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Gao Jiong restored to office.

sentences.zh: 熲、威同心協贊，政刑大小，帝無不與之謀議，然後行之。

translations.literal: Jiong and Wei worked in one mind to assist; in government and punishments, great and small, the emperor consulted with them on everything before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong and Su Wei worked in concert; on every matter of policy and law, great or small, the emperor consulted them before acting.

sentences.zh: 故革命數年，天下稱平。

translations.literal: Therefore, within a few years of the dynastic change, the realm was called at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years of the founding of Sui, the empire was widely regarded as settled and at peace.

sentences.zh: 太子左庶子盧賁，以熲、威執政，心甚不平，時柱國劉昉亦被疏忌。

translations.literal: Lu Ben, Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, because Jiong and Wei held power, was deeply resentful; at the time the Pillar of State Liu Fang was also kept at a distance and regarded with suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ben, left assistant to the crown prince, resented Gao Jiong and Su Wei's hold on power; Liu Fang, a pillar of state, was likewise sidelined and distrusted.

sentences.zh: 賁因諷昉及上柱國元諧、李詢、華州刺史張賓等謀黜熲、威，五人相與輔政。

translations.literal: Ben therefore urged Fang and the Upper Pillar of State Yuan Xie, Li Xun, Zhang Bin the governor of Huazhou, and others to plot the removal of Jiong and Wei, the five of them jointly to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ben persuaded Liu Fang, Yuan Xie, Li Xun, Zhang Bin of Huazhou, and others to plot the removal of Gao Jiong and Su Wei so that the five of them could govern together.

sentences.zh: 又以晉王廣有寵於帝，私謂太子曰：「賁欲數謁殿下，恐為上所譴，願察區區之心。

translations.literal: He also, because Prince Jin Guang was favored by the emperor, said privately to the crown prince, "Ben wishes often to call on Your Highness but fears reprimand from the emperor; I hope you will perceive my humble sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Because Prince Jin Yang Guang enjoyed the emperor's favor, Lu Ben also told the crown prince privately, "I wish to visit you often but fear the emperor's rebuke—please understand my loyal intent.

sentences.zh: 」謀洩，帝窮治其事，昉等委罪於賓、賁。

translations.literal: " The plot leaked; the emperor investigated it thoroughly, and Fang and the others shifted blame onto Bin and Ben.
translations.idiomatic: " The plot was exposed; the emperor investigated to the end, and Liu Fang's group laid the blame on Zhang Bin and Lu Ben.

sentences.zh: 公卿奏二人當死，帝以故舊，不忍誅，並除名為民。

translations.literal: The high officials memorialized that the two men deserved death; the emperor, because of old ties, could not bear to execute them and stripped them both of rank, making them commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers recommended death for the two men, but the emperor, remembering old friendship, could not bring himself to execute them and merely stripped them of office and rank.

sentences.zh: 庚子，隋詔前代品爵，悉依舊不降。

translations.literal: On the day Gengzi, Sui ordered that ranks and titles of former dynasties should all follow the old standards without reduction.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the court decreed that noble ranks from earlier dynasties would be preserved without demotion.

sentences.zh: 丁未，梁主遣其弟太宰巖入賀於隋。

translations.literal: On the day Dingwei, the Liang ruler sent his younger brother Yan, Grand Steward, to offer congratulations in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the Liang emperor sent his brother Yan, Grand Steward, to congratulate the Sui court.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛巳，隋大赦。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day Xinsi, Sui proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on xinsi in the fourth month, Sui proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，悉放太常散樂為民，仍禁雜戲。

translations.literal: On the day Wuxu, all the miscellaneous performers of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices were released to become commoners, while mixed entertainments were still forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu all miscellaneous performers attached to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices were released to civilian life, while vulgar entertainments remained banned.

sentences.zh: 6散騎常侍韋鼎、兼通直散騎常侍王瑳聘於周。

translations.literal: 6 The Regular Attendant Wei Ding and the Concurrent Regular Attendant Wang Chao were sent as envoys to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen dispatched Regular Attendant Wei Ding and Concurrent Regular Attendant Wang Chao as envoys to the Northern Zhou court.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，至長安，隋已受禪，隋主致之介國。

translations.literal: On the day Xinchou they reached Chang'an; Sui had already received the abdication, and the Sui ruler sent them on to the State of Jie.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou they reached Chang'an, only to find that Sui had already taken the throne; the new emperor sent them on to the deposed Zhou ruler in Jie.

sentences.zh: 7隋主召汾州刺史韋沖為兼散騎常侍。

translations.literal: 7 The Sui ruler summoned Wei Chong, governor of Fenzhou, to be Concurrent Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Wei Chong, governor of Fenzhou, and appointed him Concurrent Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時發稽胡築長城，汾州胡千餘人，在塗亡叛。

translations.literal: At that time the Ji Hu were being mobilized to build the Great Wall; more than a thousand Hu of Fenzhou deserted on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Hu laborers were being sent to build the Great Wall, and more than a thousand Hu from Fenzhou deserted en route.

sentences.zh: 帝召沖問計，對曰：「夷狄之性，易為反覆，皆由牧宰不稱之所致。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Chong to ask his plan; he replied, "The nature of the barbarians is easy to turn back and forth—all because the local officials are unfit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Wei Chong for advice. He replied, "Barbarians are quick to turn rebellious when their magistrates are unfit.

sentences.zh: 臣請以理綏靜，可不勞兵而定。

translations.literal: Your servant asks to pacify them by reason; without troubling the army it can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: I ask leave to pacify them by just governance—I can settle this without troops.

sentences.zh: 」帝然之，命沖綏懷叛者，月餘皆至，並赴長城之役。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved and ordered Chong to soothe and win over the deserters; within a little more than a month all came in and went together to the work on the Great Wall.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and sent Wei Chong to win the deserters back; within a month they had all returned and gone on to the wall works.

sentences.zh: 沖，□之子也。

translations.literal: Chong was a son of [Yun].
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chong was a son of Wei Yun.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊午，隋封邗公雄為廣平王，永康公弘為河間王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day Wuwu, Sui enfeoffed the Duke of Han, Xiong, as Prince of Guangping, and the Duke of Yongkang, Hong, as Prince of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuwu, Yang Xiong, Duke of Han, was created Prince of Guangping, and Yang Hong, Duke of Yongkang, Prince of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 雄，高祖之族子也。

translations.literal: Xiong was a clansman son of the High Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong was a clansman of the founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 隋主潛害周靜帝而為之舉哀，葬於恭陵；

translations.literal: The Sui ruler secretly harmed the Zhou Emperor Jing but held mourning for him and buried him at Gongling;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the Zhou Emperor Jing murdered in secret, then staged mourning and buried him at Gongling;

sentences.zh: 以其族人洛為嗣。

translations.literal: he made his clansman Luo the heir.
translations.idiomatic: he installed a Yuwen clansman, Luo, as heir to the line.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸未，隋詔郊廟冕服必依《禮經》。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day Guiwei, Sui ordered that suburban and temple robes and caps must follow the Rites Classic.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guiwei, an edict required suburban and temple vestments to follow the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 其朝會之服、旗幟、犧牲皆尚赤，戎服以黃，常服通用雜色。

translations.literal: Court audience dress, banners, and sacrificial victims all favored red; military dress used yellow; ordinary dress generally used mixed colors.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress, banners, and sacrificial victims were to be red; military dress yellow; everyday dress might use various colors.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙卯，隋主始服黃，百僚畢賀。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Yimao, the Sui ruler first wore yellow; all the officials congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on yimao in the seventh month, the emperor first wore yellow robes, and the whole court offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 於是百官常服，同於庶人，皆著黃袍。

translations.literal: Thereupon the regular dress of officials, the same as that of commoners, was all to wear yellow robes.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' everyday dress, like that of commoners, became the yellow robe.

sentences.zh: 隋主朝服亦如之，唯以十三環帶為異。

translations.literal: The Sui ruler's court dress was likewise, distinguished only by a belt with thirteen rings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's court dress was the same, distinguished only by a thirteen-ring belt.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬午，隋廢東京官。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day Renwu, Sui abolished the Eastern Capital offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renwu, the Eastern Capital bureaucracy was abolished.

sentences.zh: 8吐谷渾寇涼州，隋主遣行軍元帥樂安公元諧等步騎數萬擊之。

translations.literal: 8 The Tuyuhun raided Liangzhou; the Sui ruler sent the campaign commander Yuan Xie, Prince of Le'an, with several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun raided Liangzhou; the emperor sent campaign commander Yuan Xie, Prince of Le'an, with tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry against them.

sentences.zh: 諧擊破吐谷渾於豐利山，又敗其太子可博汗於青海，俘斬萬計。

translations.literal: Xie defeated the Tuyuhun at Mount Fengli and again defeated their crown prince Kebohan at Qinghai; captives and heads numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xie routed the Tuyuhun at Mount Fengli and defeated Crown Prince Kebohan at Qinghai Lake, taking or killing tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾震駭，其王侯三十人各帥所部來降。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun were shaken in terror; thirty of their kings and marquises each led their followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, thirty Tuyuhun princes led their followers in surrender.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾可汗誇呂帥親兵遠循。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun khan Kualü led his personal troops far away in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Khan Kualü of Tuyuhun fled far away with his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 隋主以其高寧王移茲裒為河南王，使統降眾。

translations.literal: The Sui ruler made their King of Gaoning, Yizibei, Prince of Henan, and had him command the surrendered masses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Yizibei, King of Gaoning, Prince of Henan and put him in charge of the surrendered tribes.

sentences.zh: 以元諧為寧州刺史，留行軍總管賀婁子干鎮涼州。

translations.literal: He made Yuan Xie governor of Ningzhou and left the campaign commander Helou Zigan to garrison Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xie was made governor of Ningzhou, and campaign commander Helou Zigan was left to garrison Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 9九月，庚午，將軍周羅□攻隋故墅，拔之。

translations.literal: 9 In the ninth month, on the day Gengwu, the general Zhou Luo[houdi] attacked the old Sui stockade and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengwu, General Zhou Luohou attacked an old Sui outpost and captured it.

sentences.zh: 蕭摩訶攻江北。

translations.literal: Xiao Mohe attacked the north of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mohe raided the north bank of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 10隋奉車都尉於宣敏奉使巴、蜀還，奏稱：「蜀土沃饒，人物殷阜。

translations.literal: 10 Yu Xuanmin, Commandant of the Imperial Carriage of Sui, returning from a mission to Ba and Shu, memorialized, saying, "The land of Shu is fertile and rich, its people numerous and prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Xuanmin, Commandant of the Imperial Carriage, returned from a mission to Ba and Shu, he reported, "Shu is fertile and populous,

sentences.zh: 周德之衰，遂成戎首。

translations.literal: When Zhou virtue declined, it became the head of the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: and when Zhou power waned it became a center of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 宜樹建籓屏，封殖子孫。

translations.literal: It is fitting to set up a screen of feudatories and enfeoff descendants there.
translations.idiomatic: A princely fief should be established there and entrusted to the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 」隋主善之。

translations.literal: " The Sui ruler approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以越王秀為益州總管，改封蜀王。

translations.literal: On the day Xinwei, he made Prince Yue Xiu regional commander of Yizhou and changed his enfeoffment to Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Prince Yue Yang Xiu was made regional commander of Yizhou and renamed Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 宣敏，謹之孫也。

translations.literal: Xuanmin was a grandson of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xuanmin was a grandson of Yu Jin.

sentences.zh: 壬申，隋以上柱國長孫覽、元景山並為行軍元帥，發兵入寇；

translations.literal: On the day Renshen, Sui made the Upper Pillars of State Zhangsun Lan and Yuan Jingshan both campaign commanders and sent troops to invade;
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Zhangsun Lan and Yuan Jingshan, both pillars of state, were made campaign commanders and sent to invade Chen;

sentences.zh: 命尚書左僕射高熲節度諸軍。

translations.literal: he ordered Gao Jiong, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, to coordinate all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was placed in overall command.

sentences.zh: 初，周、齊所鑄錢凡四等，及民間私錢，名品甚眾，輕重不等。

translations.literal: Earlier, the coin cast by Zhou and Qi totaled four grades, and among private coin of the people the names and types were very numerous, their weight and value unequal.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou and Qi had minted coins in four grades, and private coinage proliferated with inconsistent weight and value.

sentences.zh: 隋主患之，更鑄五銖錢，背、面、好、肉皆有周郭，每一千重四斤二兩。

translations.literal: The Sui ruler was troubled by this and recast wuzhu coins; back, face, hole, and rim all had outer rims; every thousand weighed four jin and two liang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remedied this by minting new wuzhu coins with raised rims on both sides and around the hole; a thousand coins weighed four jin two liang.

sentences.zh: 悉禁古錢及私錢。

translations.literal: All old coin and private coin were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Old and private coinage were banned outright.

sentences.zh: 置樣於關；

translations.literal: Samples were set up at the passes;
translations.idiomatic: Standard samples were posted at frontier passes;

sentences.zh: 不如樣者，沒官銷毀之。

translations.literal: those not matching the sample were confiscated by the government and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: coin not matching the sample was confiscated and melted down.

sentences.zh: 自是錢幣始壹，民間便之。

translations.literal: From this the currency was first unified, and the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: From then on currency was unified, to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 隋鄭譯以上柱國歸第，賞賜豐厚。

translations.literal: Zheng Yi of Sui, an Upper Pillar of State, returned to his residence with rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi, a pillar of state, retired to his estate with lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 譯自以被疏，呼道士醮章祈福，為婢所告，以為巫蠱，譯又與母別居，為憲司所劾，由是除名。

translations.literal: Yi himself thought he had been kept at a distance; he called in a Daoist to perform ritual documents for blessing, was reported by a maid as practicing witchcraft, and because he also lived apart from his mother was impeached by the censorate—therefore his name was struck.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling sidelined, he had Daoist rites performed for good fortune; a maid reported him for sorcery, and because he lived apart from his mother the censorate impeached him and he was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 隋主下詔曰：「譯若留之於世，在人為不道之臣；

translations.literal: The Sui ruler issued an edict saying, "If Yi is kept in the world, among men he is an unprincipled minister;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's edict read, "If Zheng Yi remains among the living, he is an unprincipled minister to mankind;

sentences.zh: 戮之於朝，入地為不孝之鬼。

translations.literal: if executed at court, in the underworld he becomes an unfilial ghost.
translations.idiomatic: if executed at court, he becomes an unfilial ghost in the underworld.

sentences.zh: 有累幽顯，無所置之。

translations.literal: He burdens both the hidden and the manifest; there is nowhere to place him.
translations.idiomatic: He wrongs both the living and the dead; there is no fitting course.

sentences.zh: 宜賜以《孝經》，令其熟讀。

translations.literal: It is fitting to bestow on him the Classic of Filial Piety and order him to read it thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be given the Classic of Filial Piety and made to study it thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 」仍遣與母共居。

translations.literal: " He was still sent to live together with his mother.
translations.idiomatic: " He was ordered to live with his mother again.

sentences.zh: 初，周法比於齊律，煩而不要，隋主命高熲、鄭譯及上柱國楊素、率更令裴政等更加修定。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhou law compared with Qi statutes was troublesome and not essential; the Sui ruler ordered Gao Jiong, Zheng Yi, the Upper Pillar of State Yang Su, the Director of the Directorate of Astronomy Pei Zheng, and others further to revise and fix it.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou law, modeled on Qi statutes, was cumbersome; the emperor ordered Gao Jiong, Zheng Yi, Yang Su, Pei Zheng of the Directorate of Astronomy, and others to revise it.

sentences.zh: 政練習典故，達於從政，乃采魏、晉舊律，下至齊、梁，沿革重輕，取其折衷。

translations.literal: Zheng was practiced in precedents and skilled in administration; he then drew on the old laws of Wei and Jin down to Qi and Liang, tracing changes in severity and lightness, and took a balanced mean.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zheng, versed in precedent and administration, drew on codes from Wei and Jin through Qi and Liang and struck a balanced standard.

sentences.zh: 時同修者十餘人，凡有疑滯，皆取決於政。

translations.literal: At the time more than ten persons jointly revised; whenever there was doubt or blockage, all turned to Zheng for decision.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten scholars worked on the code; every doubtful point was settled by Pei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 於是去前世梟、轘及鞭法，自非謀叛以上，無收族之罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon they removed from former ages the methods of exposure, quartering, and flogging; except for plotting rebellion and above, there was no crime of punishing the whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: They abolished display of severed heads, dismemberment, and flogging as capital punishments, and ended clan extermination except for treason.

sentences.zh: 始制死刑二，絞、斬；

translations.literal: They first established two capital punishments: strangulation and decapitation;
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment was limited to strangulation and decapitation;

sentences.zh: 流刑三，自二千里至三千里；

translations.literal: three grades of exile, from two thousand li to three thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: exile in three grades from two thousand to three thousand li;

sentences.zh: 徒刑五，自一年至三年；

translations.literal: five grades of penal servitude, from one year to three years;
translations.idiomatic: forced labor in five grades from one to three years;

sentences.zh: 杖刑五，自六十至百；

translations.literal: five grades of beating with the staff, from sixty to a hundred;
translations.idiomatic: beating with the staff in five grades from sixty to a hundred strokes;

sentences.zh: 笞刑五，自十至五十。

translations.literal: five grades of beating with the light stick, from ten to fifty.
translations.idiomatic: and blows with the light stick in five grades from ten to fifty.

sentences.zh: 又制議、請、減、贖、官當之科以優士大夫。

translations.literal: They also established the categories of deliberation, plea, reduction, ransom, and official substitution to favor scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions for deliberation, plea, mitigation, commutation, and official rank in lieu of punishment favored the gentry.

sentences.zh: 除前世訊囚酷法，考掠不得過二百；

translations.literal: They removed the harsh methods of interrogating prisoners from former ages; examination under torture could not exceed two hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Harsh interrogation methods were abolished; torture in examination could not exceed two hundred blows;

sentences.zh: 枷杖大小，咸有程式。

translations.literal: the size of cangues and staffs all had fixed rules.
translations.idiomatic: and the dimensions of cangues and staffs were standardized.

sentences.zh: 民有枉屈，縣不為理者，聽以次經郡及州省；

translations.literal: If the people suffered injustice and the county would not judge it, they were allowed in turn to go through the prefecture and the provincial offices;
translations.idiomatic: If a subject was wronged and the county would not act, he might appeal up through prefecture and province;

sentences.zh: 若仍不為理，聽詣闕伸訴。

translations.literal: if still there was no judgment, they were allowed to go to the court to state their grievance.
translations.idiomatic: and if still denied justice, to petition at the capital.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊子，始行新律。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day Wuzi, the new code was first put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on wuzi in the tenth month, the new code took effect.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫絞以致斃，斬則殊形，除惡之體，於斯已極。

translations.literal: The edict said, "Strangulation brings death; decapitation separates the form—the substance of removing evil reaches its limit here.
translations.idiomatic: The edict declared, "Strangulation brings death; decapitation severs the body—punishment for evil need go no further.

sentences.zh: 梟首、轘身，義無所取，不益懲肅之理，徒表安忍之杯。

translations.literal: Exposing the head and quartering the body have nothing to be taken from in principle; they do not add to the reason of warning and awe, but only display a heart of cruel forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Displaying heads and dismembering corpses serve no just purpose, add nothing to deterrence, and only reveal cruelty.

sentences.zh: 鞭之為用，殘剝膚體，徹骨侵肌，酷均臠切。

translations.literal: The use of the whip flays and strips the skin and flesh, penetrating bone and invading muscle—its cruelty equals cutting in pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Flogging flays the flesh to the bone—cruelty equal to butchery.

sentences.zh: 雖雲遠古之式，事乖仁者之刑。

translations.literal: Although it is called a method of remote antiquity, in practice it departs from the punishments of the benevolent.
translations.idiomatic: Though called an ancient practice, it is unworthy of humane government.

sentences.zh: 梟、轘及鞭，並令去之。

translations.literal: Exposure, quartering, and the whip are all ordered removed.
translations.idiomatic: Exposure, dismemberment, and flogging as capital punishments are abolished.

sentences.zh: 貴礪帶之書，不當徒罰；

translations.literal: Those who honor the book on the whetstone and belt should not suffer penal servitude;
translations.idiomatic: Men who bear noble rank should not suffer penal servitude;

sentences.zh: 廣軒冕之廕，旁及諸親。

translations.literal: extend the shade of chariot and coronet to reach collateral kin.
translations.idiomatic: and the privilege of rank should extend to their kin.

sentences.zh: 流役六年，改為五載；

translations.literal: Exile labor of six years is changed to five;
translations.idiomatic: Exile labor of six years is reduced to five;

sentences.zh: 刑徒三歲，變從三祀。

translations.literal: penal servitude of three years is altered to follow three annual sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: and penal servitude of three years is adjusted accordingly.

sentences.zh: 其餘以輕代重，化死為生，條目甚多，備於簡策。

translations.literal: The rest replace the heavy with the light and transform death into life—the articles are very numerous and fully set down in the written records.
translations.idiomatic: Many other provisions lighten penalties and commute death sentences; the full text is recorded in the code.

sentences.zh: 雜格、嚴科，並宜除削。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous statutes and severe categories should all be cut away.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous harsh statutes are to be struck out.

sentences.zh: 」自是法制遂定，後世多遵用之。

translations.literal: " From this the legal system was settled, and later ages mostly followed and used it.
translations.idiomatic: " From this the legal system was fixed, and later dynasties largely followed it.

sentences.zh: 隋主嘗怒一郎，於殿前笞之。

translations.literal: The Sui ruler once grew angry at a gentleman and beat him with the light stick before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor, angry at a court gentleman, had him beaten in the hall.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫劉行本進曰：「此人素清，其過又小，願少寬之。

translations.literal: The Remonstrating and Advising Grandee Liu Xingben advanced and said, "This man has always been pure, and his fault is small; I wish you would lighten it a little.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating Adviser Liu Xingben stepped forward: "This man has always been upright, and his fault is slight—I beg you to show leniency.

sentences.zh: 」帝不顧。

translations.literal: " The emperor paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ignored him.

sentences.zh: 行本於是正當帝前曰：「陛下不以臣不肖，置臣左右，臣言若是，陛下安得不聽；

translations.literal: Xingben then stood directly before the emperor and said, "Your Majesty, not thinking your servant unworthy, placed him at your side; if your servant's words are right, how can Your Majesty not listen?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xingben then faced the emperor squarely: "Your Majesty placed me at your side despite my unworthiness; if I speak rightly, how can you refuse to listen?

sentences.zh: 若非，當致之於理。

translations.literal: If not, your servant should be brought to judgment.
translations.idiomatic: If I am wrong, hand me over to the law.

sentences.zh: 豈得輕臣而不顧也？

translations.literal: How can you lightly disregard your servant?
translations.idiomatic: How can you dismiss your adviser so lightly?

sentences.zh: 」因置笏於地而退。

translations.literal: " He thereupon set his tablet on the ground and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " He laid down his court tablet and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝斂容謝之。

translations.literal: The emperor composed his expression and apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor collected himself and apologized.

sentences.zh: 遂原所笞者。

translations.literal: He then pardoned the one who had been beaten.
translations.idiomatic: He then pardoned the man who had been beaten.

sentences.zh: 行本，璠之兄子也。

translations.literal: Xingben was a nephew of Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xingben was a nephew of Liu Fan.

sentences.zh: 獨孤皇后，家世貴盛而能謙恭，雅好讀書，言事多與隋主意合，帝甚寵憚之，宮中稱為「二聖」。

translations.literal: Empress Dugu, though her family for generations was noble and grand, could be modest and respectful; she elegantly loved reading; in speaking of affairs she often agreed with the Sui ruler's mind; the emperor greatly favored and stood in awe of her; within the palace they were called the "Two Sages."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dugu came from a great house yet remained modest, loved books, and often agreed with the emperor's views; he cherished and respected her, and the palace called them the "Two Sages."

sentences.zh: 帝每臨朝，後輒與帝方輦而進，至閣乃止。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor attended court, the empress always advanced side by side with him in the same carriage until they reached the gate pavilion and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor held court, the empress rode beside him in the same carriage as far as the gate pavilion.

sentences.zh: 使宦官伺帝，政有所失，隨則匡諫。

translations.literal: She sent eunuchs to watch the emperor; whenever in government there was a fault, she at once corrected and remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: She stationed eunuchs to watch him and remonstrated whenever he erred in policy.

sentences.zh: 候帝退朝。

translations.literal: She waited for the emperor to leave court.
translations.idiomatic: When court ended,

sentences.zh: 同反燕寢。

translations.literal: Together they returned to the sleeping chamber.
translations.idiomatic: they returned together to the inner apartments.

sentences.zh: 有司奏稱：「《周禮》：百官之妻，命於王后，請依古制。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized, saying, "The Rites of Zhou: the wives of the hundred officials receive appointment from the queen—we ask to follow the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized: "The Rites of Zhou provide that officials' wives receive appointment from the queen—we ask to restore this ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 」後曰：「婦人預政，或從此為漸，不可開其源也。

translations.literal: The empress said: "For a woman to take part in government—even if it were to begin from this—one must not open the source of it."
translations.idiomatic: The empress replied: "If women begin to meddle in government, even from a small start like this, the floodgate must not be opened."

sentences.zh: 」大都督崔長仁，後之中外兄弟也，犯法當斬，帝以後故，欲免其罪。

translations.literal: Grand Commander Cui Changren, a brother of the empress by marriage within and without the clan, violated the law and deserved execution; the emperor, for the empress's sake, wished to pardon his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commander Cui Changren, a brother-in-law of the empress, had broken the law and was liable to execution; because of the empress, the emperor wanted to spare him.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「國家之事，焉可顧私！

translations.literal: The empress said: "Affairs of the state—how can one consider private ties!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "State business cannot be bent for private affection!"

sentences.zh: 」長仁竟坐死。

translations.literal: Changren in the end was punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: Changren was executed after all.

sentences.zh: 後性儉約，帝嘗合止利藥，須胡粉一兩。

translations.literal: The empress by nature was frugal; the emperor once compounded a medicine to stop benefit to the stomach and needed one liang of foreign powder.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was frugal by nature. Once, when the emperor was preparing a digestive medicine, he needed an ounce of lead powder.

sentences.zh: 宮內不用，求之，竟不得。

translations.literal: Within the palace it was not used; they sought it and in the end could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: The palace did not keep it, and a search failed to turn any up.

sentences.zh: 又欲賜柱國劉嵩妻織成衣領，宮內亦無之。

translations.literal: He also wished to bestow on the wife of the Pillar of State Liu Song a brocade collar for a garment, and within the palace there was none of that either.
translations.idiomatic: He also wanted to give Pillar of State Liu Song's wife a brocade garment collar, but the palace had none of those either.

sentences.zh: 然帝懲周氏之失，不以權任假借外戚，後兄弟不過將軍、刺史。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor took warning from the Zhou house's failures and did not lend power and office to maternal kin; the empress's brothers rose no higher than general or regional governor.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of how the Zhou had fallen through overmighty consort clans, the emperor refused to entrust power to his wife's relatives; her brothers never rose above general or governor.

sentences.zh: 帝外家呂氏，濟南人，素微賤。

translations.literal: The emperor's mother's family, the Lü clan, were men of Jinan and had always been low and mean.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's maternal Lü family came from Jinan and had long been humble and obscure.

sentences.zh: 齊亡以來，帝求訪，不知所在。

translations.literal: Since the Qi perished, the emperor had sought them but did not know where they were.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Qi he had searched for them without success.

sentences.zh: 及即位，始求得舅子呂永吉，追贈外祖雙周為太尉，封齊郡公，以永吉襲爵。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, he at last found his mother's nephew Lü Yongji, posthumously enfeoffed his maternal grandfather Shuang Zhou as Grand Marshal, enfeoffed him as Duke of Qi Commandery, and had Yongji inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned he located his mother's nephew Lü Yongji, posthumously honored his grandfather Shuang Zhou as Grand Marshal and Duke of Qi, and let Yongji inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 永吉從父道貴，性尤頑呆，言詞鄙陋，帝厚加供給，而不許接對朝士。

translations.literal: Yongji's paternal uncle Daogui was by nature especially dull and stupid; his words were coarse and vulgar; the emperor richly supplied him but did not allow him to meet and converse with court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji's uncle Daogui was exceptionally dull and crude in speech; the emperor supported him generously but barred him from mingling with court officials.

sentences.zh: 拜上儀同三司，出為濟南太守；

translations.literal: He was appointed Senior Master of Ceremonies, Third Rank, and sent out as governor of Jinan;
translations.idiomatic: Daogui was made a third-rank Master of Ceremonies and sent out as governor of Jinan;

sentences.zh: 後郡廢，終於家。

translations.literal: later the commandery was abolished, and he ended his life at home.
translations.idiomatic: when the commandery was later abolished he lived out his days at home.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，隋主如岐州。

translations.literal: On the day Renchen, the Sui ruler went to Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the emperor traveled to Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 岐州刺史安定梁彥光，有惠政，隋主下詔褒美，賜束帛及御傘，以厲天下之吏；

translations.literal: Liang Yanguang of Anding, governor of Qi Province, had a benevolent administration; the Sui ruler issued an edict praising him and bestowed silks and an imperial parasol, to encourage the officials of the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yanguang of Anding, governor of Qi, governed with kindness; the emperor issued an edict of praise and gave him silk and an imperial parasol as a model for officials everywhere;

sentences.zh: 久之，徙相州刺史。

translations.literal: after a long time he was transferred to be governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: later he was transferred to Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 岐俗質厚，彥光以靜鎮之，奏課連為天下最。

translations.literal: The customs of Qi were plain and thick; Yanguang governed them with quiet, and his memorials of achievement were repeatedly ranked first in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was a plain, honest region; Yanguang ruled it with quiet restraint, and his performance reports led the empire year after year.

sentences.zh: 及居相，部如岐州法。

translations.literal: When he took up office in Xiang, he governed the department by the methods used in Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiang he applied the same quiet methods he had used at Qi.

sentences.zh: 鄴自齊亡，衣冠士人多遷入關，唯工商樂戶移實州郭。

translations.literal: Since the Qi perished, gentry and scholars of Ye had for the most part moved into the Pass; only artisans, merchants, and households of musicians were moved in to fill the cities of the province.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell, Ye's gentry had largely moved into the Guanzhong region; only artisans, traders, and entertainer households were relocated to repopulate the prefectural cities.

sentences.zh: 風俗險詖，好興謠訟，目彥光為「著帽餳」。

translations.literal: The customs were treacherous and disputatious; they loved to raise ballads and lawsuits, and they called Yanguang "Congee in a Hat."
translations.idiomatic: The people were sharp-tongued and litigious, loved rumor and lawsuits, and nicknamed him "Congee in a Hat."

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，免彥光官。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he dismissed Yanguang from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, he removed Yanguang from office.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜趙州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed governor of Zhao Province.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was appointed governor of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 彥光自請復為相州，帝許之。

translations.literal: Yanguang himself requested to return to Xiang Province, and the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang asked to return to Xiang, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 豪猾聞彥光再來，皆嗤之。

translations.literal: When the powerful and crafty heard that Yanguang was coming again, they all sneered at him.
translations.idiomatic: The local bullies sneered when they heard Yanguang was coming back.

sentences.zh: 彥光至，發擿奸伏，有若神明，豪猾潛竄，闔境大治。

translations.literal: When Yanguang arrived, he exposed hidden wrongdoing as if he were a spirit; the powerful and crafty fled in secret, and the whole jurisdiction was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he uncovered hidden crimes with uncanny precision; the ringleaders fled, and the region was thoroughly pacified.

sentences.zh: 於是招致名儒，每鄉立學，親臨策試，褒勤黜怠。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned famous Confucians, established a school in every district, personally came to examine them by question, and rewarded diligence while demoting slackness.
translations.idiomatic: He then invited distinguished scholars, founded a school in every district, examined students himself, and rewarded diligence while punishing idleness.

sentences.zh: 及舉秀才，祖道於郊，以財物資之。

translations.literal: When he recommended a cultivated talent, he escorted him to the outskirts and supplied him with goods and wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he sent up a candidate for the cultivated-talent examination, he saw him off at the suburban rite and gave him travel funds.

sentences.zh: 於是風化大變，吏民感悅，無復訟者。

translations.literal: Thereupon customs greatly changed; officials and people were moved and pleased, and there were no more litigants.
translations.idiomatic: Customs were transformed; officials and commoners rejoiced, and lawsuits ceased.

sentences.zh: 時又有相州刺史陳留樊叔略，有異政，帝以璽書褒美，班示天下，征拜司農。

translations.literal: At this time there was also Fan Shulue of Chenliu, governor of Xiang Province, who had unusual administration; the emperor with an imperial-seal letter praised him, displayed it throughout the realm, and summoned him to be Minister of Public Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Fan Shulue of Chenliu, another Xiang governor noted for exceptional governance, received an imperial commendation circulated empire-wide and was summoned to head the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 新豐令房恭懿，政為三輔之最，帝賜以粟帛。

translations.literal: Fang Gongyi, magistrate of Xinfeng, had administration ranked highest in the three metropolitan circuits; the emperor bestowed grain and silks on him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Gongyi, magistrate of Xinfeng, ranked first among the capital-region counties and received grain and silk from the throne.

sentences.zh: 雍州諸縣令朝謁，帝見恭懿，必呼至榻前，訪以治民之術。

translations.literal: When the magistrates of Yong Province came to audience, whenever the emperor saw Gongyi he always called him before the couch and inquired into his methods of governing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yong prefecture magistrates attended court, the emperor would call Gongyi to his couch and ask how he governed his people.

sentences.zh: 累遷德州司馬。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to be Vice Governor of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to vice governor of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 帝謂諸州朝集使曰：「房恭懿志存體國，愛養我民，此乃上天宗廟之所祐。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the envoys assembled from the provinces: "Fang Gongyi's will is set on cherishing the state as a whole and lovingly nurturing my people—this is what Heaven and the imperial ancestors bless."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the provincial envoys at court: "Fang Gongyi cares for the whole realm and nurtures my people—Heaven and our ancestors smile on such men."

sentences.zh: 朕若置而不賞，上天宗廟必當責我。

translations.literal: If I set him aside and do not reward him, Heaven and the imperial ancestors will surely blame me.
translations.idiomatic: If I fail to reward him, Heaven and the ancestors will hold me to account.

sentences.zh: 卿等宜師範之。

translations.literal: You gentlemen ought to take him as a model.
translations.idiomatic: You should all take him as your model.

sentences.zh: 」因擢為海州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was promoted to be governor of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to governor of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 由是州縣吏多稱職，百姓富庶。

translations.literal: From this, officials of provinces and districts for the most part fulfilled their duties, and the common people were rich and secure.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter local officials generally performed well, and the people grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁卯，隋遣兼散騎侍郎鄭摠來聘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day Dingmao, Sui sent the Concurrent Master of the Palace Gate for Diplomatic Reception Zheng Can on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingmao, Sui dispatched Master of Diplomatic Reception Zheng Can on a friendly embassy.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚子，隋主還長安，復鄭譯官爵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day Gengzi, the Sui ruler returned to Chang'an and restored Zheng Yi's office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengzi, the emperor returned to Chang'an and restored Zheng Yi's titles.

sentences.zh: 11廣州刺史馬靖，得嶺表人心，兵甲精練，數有戰功。

translations.literal: 11 The Governor of Guangzhou Ma Jing had won the hearts of the people beyond the ranges; his weapons and armor were refined, and he had repeatedly achieved merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: 11 Ma Jing, governor of Guangzhou, had won the loyalty of the Lingnan region; his troops were well trained and he had won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 朝廷疑之，遣吏部侍郎蕭引觀靖舉措，諷令送質，外托收督賧物，引至番禺。

translations.literal: The court was suspicious of him and sent Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Xiao Yin to observe Jing's conduct, hinting that he should send hostages; outwardly it was to collect and supervise tribute goods, and Yin arrived at Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: The court grew wary and sent Vice Minister Xiao Yin to watch him and suggest he send hostages to the capital, ostensibly to collect tribute; Yin reached Panyu.

sentences.zh: 靖即遣子弟入質。

translations.literal: Jing at once sent his sons and younger brothers in as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Jing promptly sent his sons and nephews to court as hostages.

sentences.zh: 12是歲，隋主詔境內之民任聽出家，仍令計口出錢，營造經像。

translations.literal: 12 In this year the Sui ruler issued an edict that the people within the borders might, as they wished, leave the laity and become monks, and still ordered a levy per mouth to raise funds to build sutras and images.
translations.idiomatic: 12 That year the emperor decreed that anyone in the realm might take Buddhist orders, while also levying a per-capita tax to fund scriptures and images.

sentences.zh: 於是時俗從風而靡，民間佛書，多於《六經》數十百倍。

translations.literal: Thereupon the fashion of the time followed the wind and was swept away; Buddhist books among the people were many times more numerous than the Six Classics by tens and hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: The fashion spread until Buddhist texts in private hands outnumbered the Confucian classics many times over.

sentences.zh: 13突厥佗缽可汗病且卒，謂其子庵邏曰：「吾兄不立其子，委位於我。

translations.literal: 13 The Türk Tabo Qaghan was ill and near death; he said to his son Anluo: "My elder brother did not establish his son but entrusted the position to me.
translations.idiomatic: 13 Tabo Qaghan of the Turks fell mortally ill and told his son Anluo: "My brother did not enthrone his own son but gave me the khanship.

sentences.zh: 我死，汝曹當避大邏便。

translations.literal: When I die, you all should avoid Daluobian."
translations.idiomatic: When I die, you must keep clear of Daluobian."

sentences.zh: 」及卒，國人將立大邏便。

translations.literal: When he died, the people of the state were about to establish Daluobian.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the tribes prepared to raise Daluobian.

sentences.zh: 以其母賤，眾不服；

translations.literal: Because his mother was lowborn, the multitude would not submit;
translations.idiomatic: His mother was of low birth, and the tribes refused to accept him;

sentences.zh: 庵邏實貴，突厥素重之。

translations.literal: Anluo was truly noble, and the Turks had always respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Anluo was of high birth and had long been held in esteem.

sentences.zh: 攝圖最後至，謂國人曰：「若立庵邏者，我當帥兄弟事之。

translations.literal: Shetu arrived last and said to the people of the state: "If you establish Anluo, I shall lead my brothers to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Shetu arrived last and told the assembly: "If you choose Anluo, my brothers and I will serve him.

sentences.zh: 若立大邏便，我必守境，利刃長矛以相待。

translations.literal: If you establish Daluobian, I shall certainly hold the border and meet you with sharp blades and long spears."
translations.idiomatic: If you choose Daluobian, I will hold the frontier and meet you with blade and spear."

sentences.zh: 」攝圖長，且雄勇，國人莫敢拒，竟立庵邏為嗣。

translations.literal: Shetu was the eldest and moreover bold and brave; the people of the state did not dare refuse, and in the end they established Anluo as successor.
translations.idiomatic: Shetu was the eldest and a formidable warrior; no one dared oppose him, and Anluo was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 大邏便不得立，心不服庵邏，每遣人詈辱之。

translations.literal: Daluobian could not be established; in his heart he did not submit to Anluo and repeatedly sent men to revile and insult him.
translations.idiomatic: Daluobian was passed over and, resentful, repeatedly sent men to insult Anluo.

sentences.zh: 庵邏不能制，因以國讓攝圖。

translations.literal: Anluo could not control him and therefore yielded the state to Shetu.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to restrain him, Anluo yielded the khanship to Shetu.

sentences.zh: 國中相與議曰：「四可汗子，攝圖最賢。

translations.literal: Within the state they deliberated together, saying: "Of the four sons of the qaghan, Shetu is the most worthy."
translations.idiomatic: The tribes agreed: "Of the late qaghan's four sons, Shetu is the finest."

sentences.zh: 」共迎立之，號沙缽略可汗，居都斤山。

translations.literal: Together they welcomed and established him, titled him Qaghan Shaboluo, and he dwelt at Mount Dujin.
translations.idiomatic: They raised him as Shaboluo Qaghan on Mount Dujin.

sentences.zh: 庵邏降居獨洛水，稱第二可汗。

translations.literal: Anluo withdrew to dwell on the Duluo River and styled himself Second Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Anluo withdrew to the Duluo River as Second Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 大邏便乃謂沙缽略曰：「我與爾俱可汗子，各承父後。

translations.literal: Daluobian then said to Shaboluo: "You and I are both sons of the qaghan, each inheriting after our fathers.
translations.idiomatic: Daluobian protested to Shaboluo: "We are both the qaghan's sons, each heir to his father's line.

sentences.zh: 爾今極尊，我獨無位，何也？

translations.literal: You are now supremely honored while I alone have no position—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Why are you supreme while I have no standing?"

sentences.zh: 」沙缽略患之，以為阿波可汗，還領所部。

translations.literal: Shaboluo was troubled by this and made him Qaghan Apo, returning him to lead his own following.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo, uneasy, named him Apo Qaghan and sent him back to his own tribes.

sentences.zh: 又沙缽略從父玷厥，居西面，號達頭可汗。

translations.literal: Moreover Shaboluo's paternal uncle Dianjue dwelt in the west and was titled Qaghan Datou.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo's uncle Dianjue held the west as Datou Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 諸可汗各統部眾，分居四面。

translations.literal: The various qaghans each commanded their followings and dwelt apart on the four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Each khan ruled his own followers on a separate quarter of the steppe.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略勇而得眾，北方皆畏附之。
