translations.literal: Shaboluo was brave and won the multitude; the north all feared and attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo was bold and popular; the northern peoples feared and followed him.

sentences.zh: 隋主既立，待突厥禮薄，突厥大怨。

translations.literal: After the Sui ruler had been established, he treated the Turks with thin ceremony, and the Turks were greatly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, the Sui emperor treated the Turks with scant ceremony, and they resented it deeply.

sentences.zh: 千金公主傷其宗祀覆沒，日夜言於沙缽略，請為周室復讎。

translations.literal: The Princess Qianjin grieved that her ancestral sacrifices were overthrown; day and night she spoke to Shaboluo, asking to take revenge for the Zhou house.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Qianjin, mourning the fall of her Zhou lineage, pressed Shaboluo day and night to avenge the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略謂其臣曰：「我，周之親也。

translations.literal: Shaboluo said to his ministers: "I am kin to the Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo told his ministers: "I am the Zhou emperor's kinsman.

sentences.zh: 今隋公自立而不能制，復何面目見可賀敦乎！

translations.literal: Now the Duke of Sui has set himself up and I cannot control him—what face have I to show the Khatun!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Sui duke has seized power and I cannot stop him—how can I face the Khatun?"

sentences.zh: 」乃與故齊營州刺史高寶寧合兵為寇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he joined forces with Gao Baoning, former governor of Ying Province under the former Qi, to raid as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He then allied with Gao Baoning, the former Qi governor of Ying, and raided the border.

sentences.zh: 隋主患之，敕緣邊修保障，峻長城，命上柱國武威陰壽鎮幽州，京兆尹虞慶則鎮并州，屯兵數萬以備之。

translations.literal: The Sui ruler was troubled by this and ordered the border regions to repair defenses and heighten the Long Wall; he appointed the Pillar of State Yin Shou of Wuwei to guard You Province and the Metropolitan Governor Yu Qingze to guard Bing Province, stationing tens of thousands of troops to prepare against them.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the emperor strengthened frontier defenses and the Great Wall, posted Pillar of State Yin Shou at Youzhou and Metropolitan Governor Yu Qingze at Bingzhou, and massed tens of thousands of troops along the border.

sentences.zh: 初，奉車都尉長孫晟送千金公主入突厥，突厥可汗愛其善射，留之竟歲，命諸子弟貴人與之親友，冀得其射法。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Commandant of the Imperial Carriages Zhangsun Sheng had escorted Princess Qianjin into the Turks; the Türk qaghan loved his skill in archery, kept him a full year, and ordered the qaghan's sons, younger brothers, and nobles to befriend him, hoping to obtain his method of shooting.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chief Commandant Zhangsun Sheng had escorted Princess Qianjin to the Turks; the qaghan admired his archery, detained him a year, and had princes and nobles befriend him to learn his technique.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略弟處羅侯，號突利設，尤得眾心，為沙缽略所忌，密托心腹陰與晟盟。

translations.literal: Shaboluo's younger brother Chuluohou, titled Tuli Shad, especially won the hearts of the people and was envied by Shaboluo; he secretly entrusted a trusted man to ally with Sheng in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo's brother Chuluohou, titled Tuli Shad, was especially popular and aroused Shaboluo's jealousy; through a trusted agent he secretly allied with Sheng.

sentences.zh: 晟與之遊獵，因察山川形勢，部眾強弱，靡不知之。

translations.literal: Sheng hunted with him and thereby observed the mountains and rivers, terrain, strength and weakness of the followings—there was nothing he did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting with him, Sheng mapped the terrain and gauged every tribe's strength.

sentences.zh: 及突厥入寇，晟上書曰：「今諸夏雖安，戎虜尚梗，興師致討，未是其時，棄於度外，又相侵擾，故宜密運籌策，有以攘之。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided, Sheng memorialized, saying: "Now the various Xia are at peace, but the barbarian Rong still obstruct; to raise troops and deliver punishment is not yet the time, yet to abandon them beyond the bounds and again suffer their raids—therefore one should secretly devise plans to have means to repel them."
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks invaded, Sheng wrote: "The empire is at peace, but the barbarians remain a threat; a major campaign is premature, yet we cannot ignore their raids—we must undermine them by secret strategy."

sentences.zh: 玷厥之於攝圖，兵強而位下，外名相屬，內隙已彰；

translations.literal: Dianjue toward Shetu: troops strong yet rank low; outwardly their names are linked, but inwardly their rift is already clear;
translations.idiomatic: Dianjue is strong in troops but low in rank; though nominally subordinate to Shetu, the rift is already plain;

sentences.zh: 鼓動其情，必將自戰。

translations.literal: if one stirs his feelings, he will surely turn to fighting on his own.
translations.idiomatic: stir his ambitions and he will turn on Shetu.

sentences.zh: 又，處羅侯者，攝圖之弟，奸多勢弱，曲取眾心，國人愛之，因為攝圖所忌，其心殊不自安，跡示彌縫，實懷疑懼。

translations.literal: Moreover Chuluohou is Shetu's younger brother—cunning and numerous but weak in power; he bends to win the people's hearts, and the people of the state love him; therefore he is envied by Shetu; his heart is especially ill at ease; outwardly he shows smoothing over, but in reality he harbors suspicion and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluohou, Shetu's brother, is clever but weak; he curries favor with the tribes, whom Shetu resents; outwardly conciliatory, he is inwardly fearful.

sentences.zh: 又，阿波首鼠，介在其間，頗畏攝圖，受其牽率，唯強是與，未有定心。

translations.literal: Moreover Apo is irresolute, placed between them; he quite fears Shetu, is dragged along by him, follows only the strong, and has no settled mind.
translations.idiomatic: Apo wavers between them, fears Shetu, follows whoever is stronger, and lacks firm loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今宜遠交而近攻，離強而合弱。

translations.literal: Now one should befriend those far and attack those near, separate the strong and unite with the weak.
translations.idiomatic: We should befriend distant factions, strike nearby ones, divide the strong and align with the weak.

sentences.zh: 通使玷厥，說合阿波，則攝圖回兵，自防右地。

translations.literal: Send envoys to Dianjue and persuade Apo to join him, and then Shetu will turn his troops and himself guard the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to Dianjue, win over Apo, and Shetu will have to turn back to guard his western flank.

sentences.zh: 又引處羅，遣連奚、□則攝圖分眾，還備左方。

translations.literal: Also draw in Chuluohou; dispatch connections to the Xi and the Kumo Xi—then Shetu will divide his forces and turn back to guard the left.
translations.idiomatic: Win Chuluohou as well; link the Xi and Kumo Xi against him, and Shetu will split his army to protect his left.

sentences.zh: 首尾猜嫌，腹心離阻，十數年後，乘釁討之，必可一舉而空其國矣。

translations.literal: Suspicion at head and tail, estrangement at the center—after a dozen years or so, if we seize an opening and strike, we can surely in one move empty their state.
translations.idiomatic: With their leaders suspicious and their core divided, a strike in ten years or so could destroy them in a single campaign.

sentences.zh: 」帝省表，大悅，因召與語。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and was greatly pleased; he therefore summoned him and conversed with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with delight and summoned Sheng for a long audience.

sentences.zh: 晟復口陳形勢，手畫山川，寫其虛實，皆如指掌，帝深嗟異，皆納用之。

translations.literal: Sheng again orally set forth the situation, drew the mountains and rivers with his hand, and wrote out their emptiness and fullness—all as if in the palm of his hand; the emperor deeply sighed in wonder and adopted it all.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng rehearsed the situation, sketched the terrain, and laid out each tribe's strength as clearly as if it lay in his palm; the emperor marveled and adopted every proposal.

sentences.zh: 遣太僕元暉出伊吾道，詣達頭，賜以狼頭纛。

translations.literal: He sent the Grand Master of the Stud Yuan Hui by the Yiwu road to Datou and bestowed on him a wolf-head banner.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Grand Master of the Stud Yuan Hui along the Yiwu route to Datou with a wolf-head banner.

sentences.zh: 達頭使來，引居沙缽略使上。

translations.literal: When Datou's envoy came, he was seated above Shaboluo's envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When Datou's envoy arrived at court, he was seated above Shaboluo's envoy.

sentences.zh: 以晟為車騎將軍，出黃龍道，繼幣賜奚、□、契丹，遣為鄉導，得至處羅侯所，深布心腹，誘之內附。

translations.literal: Sheng was made General of Chariots and Cavalry, went out by the Huanglong road, continued gifts to the Xi, the Kumo Xi, and the Khitan, and sent them as guides, thereby reaching Chuluohou's place; he deeply won over his inner circle and enticed him to submit inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was made General of Chariots and Cavalry, traveled the Huanglong route, lavished gifts on the Xi, Kumo Xi, and Khitan, and used them as guides until he reached Chuluohou and won his inner circle to defect.

sentences.zh: 反間既行，果相猜貳。

translations.literal: Once the stratagem of alienation was set in motion, they truly became mutually suspicious and divided.
translations.idiomatic: The disinformation campaign worked, and the Turks soon turned on one another.

sentences.zh: 14始興王叔陵，太子之次弟也，與太子異母，母曰彭貴人。

translations.literal: 14 Prince Shixing Shulang, the crown prince's next younger brother, was not born of the same mother as the crown prince; his mother was the Honored Lady Peng.
translations.idiomatic: 14 Prince Shixing Shulang, the crown prince's younger brother, had a different mother, Lady Peng.

sentences.zh: 叔陵為江州刺史，性苛刻狡險。

translations.literal: Shulang was governor of Jiang Province; by nature he was harsh, harsh, crafty, and dangerous.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Jiang he was harsh, cunning, and ruthless.

sentences.zh: 新安王伯固，以善諧謔，有寵於上及太子；

translations.literal: Prince Xin'an Bogu, because he was skilled in witty banter, had favor with the emperor and the crown prince;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin'an Bogu, a gifted wit, was a favorite of the emperor and crown prince;

sentences.zh: 叔陵疾之，陰求其過失，欲中之以法。

translations.literal: Shulang resented him and secretly sought his faults, wishing to strike him down by law.
translations.idiomatic: Shulang hated him and secretly hunted for faults with which to prosecute him.

sentences.zh: 叔陵入為揚州刺史，事務多關涉省閣，執事承意順旨，即諷上進用之；

translations.literal: Shulang entered the capital as governor of Yang Province; his affairs largely impinged on the provincial offices of the capital; if the officials in charge complied with his intent, he would hint to the emperor to promote them;
translations.idiomatic: When Shulang became governor of Yang, he meddled in capital administration; officials who pleased him were recommended for promotion;

sentences.zh: 微致違忤，必抵以大罪，重者至殊死。

translations.literal: if they slightly incurred opposition, he would certainly strike them with a great crime, and in heavy cases even to execution by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: the slightest resistance brought grave charges, even execution.

sentences.zh: 伯固憚之，乃諂求其意。

translations.literal: Bogu feared him and therefore flattered him to learn his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Bogu, afraid, flattered him to learn his wishes.

sentences.zh: 叔陵好發古塚，伯固好射雉，常相從郊野，大相款狎，因密圖不軌。

translations.literal: Shulang loved to open ancient tombs; Bogu loved to shoot pheasants; they often followed each other into the suburbs and were greatly intimate, and thereby secretly plotted treason.
translations.idiomatic: Shulang loved looting ancient tombs; Bogu loved hawking; they often roamed the countryside together, grew intimate, and secretly plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 伯固為侍中，每得密語，必告叔陵。

translations.literal: Bogu was Attendant-in-Ordinary; whenever he obtained confidential words, he always told Shulang.
translations.idiomatic: As Attendant-in-Ordinary, Bogu reported every court secret to Shulang.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，己酉，上不豫，太子與始興王叔陵、長沙王叔堅並入侍疾。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, on the day Jiyou, the emperor was unwell; the crown prince and Prince Shixing Shulang and Prince of Changsha Shujian together entered to attend the illness.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on jiyou of the first month, the emperor fell ill; the crown prince, Prince Shixing Shulang, and Prince of Changsha Shujian attended him at his bedside.

sentences.zh: 叔陵陰有異志，命典藥吏曰：「切藥刀甚鈍，可礪之！

translations.literal: Shulang secretly harbored a different intent and ordered the pharmacy clerk, saying: "The medicine-cutting knife is very dull—it should be sharpened!"
translations.idiomatic: Shulang harbored treacherous designs and told the pharmacy clerk: "The medicine knife is very dull—you had better sharpen it!"

sentences.zh: 」甲寅，上殂。

translations.literal: On the day Jiayin, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 倉猝之際，叔陵命左右於外取劍。

translations.literal: In the sudden moment, Shulang ordered his attendants outside to fetch swords.
translations.idiomatic: In the confusion Shulang ordered his attendants outside to fetch swords.

sentences.zh: 左右弗悟，取朝服木劍以進，叔陵怒。

translations.literal: The attendants did not understand; they brought in the wooden sword of court dress and presented it, and Shulang was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants misunderstood and brought the ceremonial wooden sword from his court robes; Shulang flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 叔堅在側，聞之，疑有變，伺其所為。

translations.literal: Shujian was at his side; when he heard this, he suspected trouble and watched what Shulang would do.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shujian stood nearby, heard the order, sensed treachery, and watched Shulang closely.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，小斂。

translations.literal: On yimao, the initial encoffining was performed.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the body was laid out for encoffining.

sentences.zh: 太子哀哭俯伏。

translations.literal: The crown prince wept in grief and prostrated himself.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wailed and prostrated himself in mourning.

sentences.zh: 叔陵抽剉藥刀斫太子，中項，太子悶絕於地；

translations.literal: Shulang drew the medicine-grinding knife and hacked at the crown prince, striking the nape; the crown prince collapsed unconscious on the ground;
translations.idiomatic: Shulang snatched the pharmacy knife and slashed at the crown prince's neck; the prince collapsed in a heap;

sentences.zh: 母柳皇后走來救之，又斫后數下。

translations.literal: The mother, Empress Liu, ran to save him, and Shulang hacked the empress several times as well.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu rushed to shield him and was hacked several times herself.

sentences.zh: 乳媼吳氏自後掣其肘，太子乃得起；

translations.literal: The wet nurse, Lady Wu, seized his elbow from behind, and only then could the crown prince rise;
translations.idiomatic: Wet nurse Lady Wu seized Shulang's arm from behind, and the crown prince struggled to his feet;

sentences.zh: 叔陵持太子衣，太子自奮得免。

translations.literal: Shulang clutched the crown prince's garment, but the crown prince struggled free by his own exertion.
translations.idiomatic: Shulang grabbed the prince's robe, but the prince wrenched free.

sentences.zh: 叔堅手扼叔陵，奪去其刀，仍牽就柱，以其褶袖縛之。

translations.literal: Shujian seized Shulang by hand, wrested away his knife, still dragged him to a pillar, and bound him with the sleeves of his robe.
translations.idiomatic: Shujian grappled with Shulang, tore away the knife, dragged him to a pillar, and bound him with his own robe sleeves.

sentences.zh: 時吳媼已扶太子避賊，叔堅求太子所在，欲受生殺之命。

translations.literal: By then Lady Wu had already helped the crown prince flee the assailant; Shujian sought where the crown prince was, wishing to receive orders over life and death.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu had already hustled the prince to safety; Shujian searched for him, ready to accept whatever command the prince gave.

sentences.zh: 叔陵多力，奮袖得脫，突走出雲龍門，馳車還東府，召左右斷青溪道，赦東城囚以充戰士，散金帛賞賜；

translations.literal: Shulang was very strong; he shook free his sleeves and broke loose, burst out through the Cloud Dragon Gate, galloped by chariot back to the Eastern Palace, summoned his attendants to cut the Qingxi road, pardoned the prisoners of the eastern city to serve as warriors, and scattered gold and silk in reward;
translations.idiomatic: Shulang was powerfully built; he tore free, bolted out the Cloud Dragon Gate, raced to his Eastern Palace, blocked the Qingxi road, freed eastern-city prisoners for his army, and scattered gold and silk as bounty;

sentences.zh: 又遣人往新林追其所部兵；

translations.literal: He also sent men to Xinlin to recall the troops under his command;
translations.idiomatic: and sent riders to Xinlin to recall his personal troops;

sentences.zh: 仍自被甲，著白布帽，登城西門招募百姓；

translations.literal: then donned armor himself, put on a white cloth cap, and climbed the western city gate to recruit the common people;
translations.idiomatic: then armored himself, wore a white cloth cap, and mounted the western gate to recruit townspeople;

sentences.zh: 又召諸王將帥，莫有至者，唯新安王伯固單馬赴之，助叔陵指揮。

translations.literal: He also summoned the princes and generals, but none came—only Prince Xin'an Bogu came alone on horseback to join him and helped Shulang direct operations.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the princes and commanders, but only Prince Xin'an Bogu rode out alone to help him command.

sentences.zh: 叔陵兵可千人，欲據城自守。

translations.literal: Shulang's troops numbered about a thousand; he intended to hold the city and defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: With roughly a thousand men Shulang prepared to hold the capital by force.

sentences.zh: 時眾軍並緣江防守，台內空虛。

translations.literal: At that time the mass of armies were all posted along the river on guard; within the palace city it was empty.
translations.idiomatic: The main armies were deployed along the river; the palace quarter lay nearly undefended.

sentences.zh: 叔堅白柳后，使太子舍人河內司馬申，以太子命召右衛將軍蕭摩訶入見受敕，帥馬步數百趣東府，屯城西門。

translations.literal: Shujian reported to Empress Liu and had the crown prince's chamberlain Sima Shen of Henei, by the crown prince's order, summon the General of the Right Guard Xiao Mohe to an audience to receive command; Mohe led several hundred horse and foot in haste to the Eastern Palace and encamped at the western city gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shujian appealed to Empress Liu and sent the crown prince's attendant Sima Shen of Henei to summon General of the Right Guard Xiao Mohe with the prince's commission; Mohe led several hundred horse and foot to the Eastern Palace and camped at the western gate.

sentences.zh: 叔陵惶恐，遣記室韋諒送其鼓吹與摩訶，謂之曰：「事捷，必以公為台鼎。

translations.literal: Shulang was alarmed; he sent his recorder Wei Liang to present his band and drums to Mohe, saying to him: "If the affair succeeds, you will surely be made chief pillar of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In panic Shulang sent his recorder Wei Liang with his ceremonial musicians to Mohe, promising: "If I prevail, you shall be chief minister of the realm.

sentences.zh: 」摩訶紿報之曰：「須王心膂節將自來，方敢從命。

translations.literal: Mohe deceived him in reply, saying: "I must wait until the prince's trusted generals come in person—only then dare I obey the command.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe feigned agreement: "I must see the prince's own trusted generals before I can obey.

sentences.zh: 」步陵遣其所親戴溫、譚騏詣摩訶，摩訶執以送台，斬其首，徇東城。

translations.literal: Shulang sent his intimates Dai Wen and Tan Qi to Mohe; Mohe seized them and sent them to the court, beheaded them, and displayed their heads in the eastern city.
translations.idiomatic: Shulang sent his confidants Dai Wen and Tan Qi; Mohe arrested them, sent them to the court for execution, and paraded their heads through the eastern city.

sentences.zh: 叔陵自知不濟，入內，沉其妃張氏及寵妾七人於井，帥步騎數百自小航渡，欲趣新林，乘舟奔隋。

translations.literal: Shulang knew himself beyond saving; he went inside, drowned his consort Lady Zhang and seven favored concubines in a well, led several hundred foot and horse across the small ferry, wished to hurry to Xinlin, and take a boat to flee to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing defeat inevitable, Shulang drowned his consort Lady Zhang and seven favorite concubines in a well, led several hundred men across the small ferry toward Xinlin, intending to sail to Sui.

sentences.zh: 行至白楊路，為台軍所邀。

translations.literal: When he reached Baiyang Road, he was intercepted by the palace troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Baiyang Road the palace forces intercepted him.

sentences.zh: 伯固見兵至，旋避入巷，叔陵馳騎拔刃追之，伯固復還，叔陵部下多棄甲潰去。

translations.literal: When Bogu saw the soldiers arrive, he at once dodged into a lane; Shulang galloped with drawn blade in pursuit; Bogu came back again, and many of Shulang's followers cast off their armor and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Bogu tried to slip into an alley when troops appeared; Shulang chased him with drawn sword; Bogu doubled back, and many of Shulang's men threw down their armor and scattered.

sentences.zh: 摩訶馬容陳智深迎刺叔陵，僵仆，陳仲華就斬其首，伯固為亂兵所殺，自寅至巳乃定。

translations.literal: Mohe's groom Chen Zhishen met and stabbed Shulang; he fell stiff; Chen Zhonghua then beheaded him; Bogu was killed by the disorderly soldiers; from yin to si it was finally settled.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe's groom Chen Zhishen ran Shulang through; he dropped dead; Chen Zhonghua took his head; Bogu died in the melee; from yin through si order was restored.

sentences.zh: 叔陵諸子並賜死，伯固諸子宥為庶人。

translations.literal: All of Shulang's sons were granted death; Bogu's sons were spared and made commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Shulang's sons were all put to death; Bogu's sons were spared as commoners.

sentences.zh: 韋諒及前衡陽內史彭暠、咨議參軍兼記室鄭信、典簽俞公喜並伏誅。

translations.literal: Wei Liang, the former interior minister of Hengyang Peng Hao, the consulting colonel and recorder Zheng Xin, and the registry clerk Yu Gongxi were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liang, former interior minister of Hengyang Peng Hao, consulting colonel and recorder Zheng Xin, and registry clerk Yu Gongxi were all executed.

sentences.zh: 暠，叔陵舅也。

translations.literal: Hao was Shulang's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Hao was Shulang's uncle.

sentences.zh: 信、諒有寵於叔陵，常參謀議。

translations.literal: Xin and Liang were favored by Shulang and often took part in his counsels.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xin and Wei Liang had been Shulang's favorites and habitual advisers.

sentences.zh: 諒，粲之子也。

translations.literal: Liang was the son of Can.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liang was a son of Can.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，太子即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: On dingsi the crown prince ascended the imperial throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the crown prince took the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 2辛酉，隋置河北道行台於并州，以晉王廣為尚書令；

translations.literal: 2 On xinyou, Sui established the Hebei Circuit Executive at Bingzhou, appointing Prince of Jin Yang Guang as Director of the Department of State Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: 2 On xinyou Sui set up the Hebei circuit executive at Bingzhou and made Prince of Jin Yang Guang Director of the Department of State Affairs;

sentences.zh: 置西南道行台於益州，以蜀王秀為尚書令。

translations.literal: it established the Southwest Circuit Executive at Yizhou, appointing Prince of Shu Yang Xiu as Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and the Southwest circuit executive at Yizhou with Prince of Shu Yang Xiu as Director.

sentences.zh: 隋主懲周氏孤弱而亡，故使二子分蒞方面。

translations.literal: The Sui ruler took warning from the Zhou house's perishing through isolation and weakness, and therefore had his two sons each oversee a region.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that the Zhou had fallen because the throne was left isolated, the Sui emperor stationed two sons on distant fronts.

sentences.zh: 以二王年少，盛選貞良有才望者為之僚佐；

translations.literal: Because the two princes were young, he carefully selected upright men of talent and reputation to serve as their aides;
translations.idiomatic: As both princes were young, he chose men of proven integrity and ability as their staffs;

sentences.zh: 以靈州刺史王韶為並省右僕射，鴻臚卿趙郡李雄為兵部尚書，左武衛將軍朔方李徹總晉王府軍事，兵部尚書元巖為益州總管府長史。

translations.literal: he appointed Wang Shao, governor of Ling Prefecture, as Right Vice Director of the Bing circuit; Li Xiong of Zhao commandery, Minister of Ceremonies, as Minister of War; Li Che of Shuofang, General of the Left Martial Guard, to command the Jin prince's military affairs; and Yuan Yan, Minister of War, as chief administrator of the Yizhou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao became Right Vice Director on the Bing circuit, Li Xiong of Zhao commandery Minister of War, Li Che of Shuofang commander of the Jin prince's forces, and Yuan Yan chief administrator at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 王韶、李雄、元巖俱有骨鯁名，李徹前朝舊將，故用之。

translations.literal: Wang Shao, Li Xiong, and Yuan Yan all had reputations for unyielding integrity; Li Che was an old general of the previous dynasty—therefore they were used.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao, Li Xiong, and Yuan Yan were famed for blunt integrity; Li Che was a veteran of the previous regime—hence their selection.

sentences.zh: 初，李雄家世以學業自通，雄獨習騎射。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Li family for generations had advanced through scholarship; Xiong alone practiced horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: The Li clan had risen for generations through learning; Xiong alone trained in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 其兄子旦讓之曰：「非士大夫之素業也。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Dan reproached him, saying: "That is not the proper occupation of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Dan reproved him: "That is no occupation for a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 」雄曰：「自古聖賢，文武不備而能成其功業者鮮矣。

translations.literal: Xiong said: "Since antiquity, among sages and worthies, those who could accomplish their achievements without being complete in both civil and military affairs have been few.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong replied: "Since antiquity, few sages have achieved greatness without both wen and wu.

sentences.zh: 雄雖不敏，頗觀前志，但不守章句耳。

translations.literal: Though I, Xiong, am not clever, I have read the records of former ages—I simply do not cling to textual clauses, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: I may lack talent, but I have read the ancients; I simply refuse to be a commentarial pedant.

sentences.zh: 既文且武，兄何病焉！

translations.literal: Having both civil and military ability—what fault does elder brother find!"
translations.idiomatic: With both letters and arms, what fault can you find?"

sentences.zh: 」及將如並省，帝謂雄曰：「吾兒更事未多，以卿兼文武才，吾無北顧之憂矣！

translations.literal: When he was about to go to the Bing circuit, the emperor said to Xiong: "My son has little experience in affairs; with your combined civil and military talent, I have no worry for the north!"
translations.idiomatic: As Xiong was leaving for Bing, the emperor told him: "My son is still inexperienced; with your combined talents I need not fear for the north!"

sentences.zh: 二王欲為奢侈非法，韶、巖輒不奉教，或自鎖，或排閣切諫。

translations.literal: When the two princes wished to indulge in extravagance and unlawful acts, Shao and Yan would not carry out their orders—sometimes chaining themselves, sometimes bursting through the gate with stern remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When either prince sought luxury or lawlessness, Shao and Yan refused his orders—sometimes chaining themselves to the gate, sometimes forcing their way in with blunt remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 二王甚憚之，每事咨而後行，不敢違法度。

translations.literal: The two princes greatly feared them; in every matter they consulted them before acting and did not dare violate the law.
translations.idiomatic: Both princes came to fear them and consulted them before every act, no longer daring to overstep the law.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而賞之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and rewarded them.

sentences.zh: 又以秦王俊為河南道行台尚書令、洛州刺史，領關東兵。

translations.literal: He also made Prince of Qin Yang Jun Director of the Henan Circuit Executive, governor of Luo Prefecture, and commander of the eastern-pass troops.
translations.idiomatic: He also made Prince of Qin Yang Jun director of the Henan circuit executive, governor of Luo, and commander of the eastern-pass armies.

sentences.zh: 3癸亥，以長沙王叔堅為驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史；

translations.literal: 3 On guihai, Prince of Changsha Shujian was made General of Agile Cavalry, with the privilege of the same ceremonies as the Three Excellencies, and governor of Yang Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: 3 On guihai Prince of Changsha Shujian was made General of Agile Cavalry with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies and governor of Yang;

sentences.zh: 蕭摩訶為車騎將軍、南徐州刺史，封綏遠公，始興王叔陵家金帛累巨萬，悉以賜之。

translations.literal: Xiao Mohe was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and governor of South Xuzhou, enfeoffed as Duke Pacifying the Distance; the gold and silk of Prince Shixing Shulang's household piled up in vast sums—all were bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mohe became General of Chariots and Cavalry and governor of South Xuzhou, enfeoffed Duke Pacifying the Distance, and was given the entire hoard—worth millions—from Shulang's estate.

sentences.zh: 以司馬申為中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: Sima Shen was made Attendant and Master of Documents for Palace Communications.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shen was made Attendant and Master of Documents for Palace Communications.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，尊皇后為皇太后。

translations.literal: On yichou the empress was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the empress was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 時帝病創，臥承香殿，不能聽政。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was wounded and lay in the Hall of Receiving Fragrance, unable to attend to government.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor, still wounded, lay in the Hall of Receiving Fragrance and could not govern.

sentences.zh: 太后居柏梁殿，百司眾務，皆決於太后，帝創愈，乃歸政焉。

translations.literal: The empress dowager resided in the Hall of Cypress Beam; the myriad affairs of the hundred offices were all decided by the empress dowager; when the emperor's wounds healed, government was returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager occupied the Hall of Cypress Beam; all state business passed through her until the emperor recovered and resumed rule.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，封皇弟叔重為始興王，奉昭烈王祀。

translations.literal: On dingmao the emperor's younger brother Shuzhong was enfeoffed Prince of Shixing to maintain the sacrifices of Prince Zhaolie.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the emperor's brother Shuzhong was made Prince of Shixing to maintain the cult of Prince Zhaolie.

sentences.zh: 4隋元景山出漢口，遣上開府儀同三司鄧孝儒將卒四千攻甑山。

translations.literal: 4 Yuan Jingshan of Sui advanced from Hankou and sent the Senior General of the Army Deng Xiaoru with four thousand troops to attack Zengshan.
translations.idiomatic: 4 Sui's Yuan Jingshan marched out from Hankou and sent Senior General Deng Xiaoru with four thousand men against Zengshan.

sentences.zh: 鎮將軍陸綸以舟師救之，為孝儒所敗；

translations.literal: The defending general Lu Lun came with a fleet to rescue it and was defeated by Xiaoru;
translations.idiomatic: Defending general Lu Lun sailed to relieve the city and was defeated;

sentences.zh: 溳口、甑山、沌陽守將皆棄城走。

translations.literal: the garrison commanders of Yukou, Zengshan, and Dunyang all abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: the garrisons at Yukou, Zengshan, and Dunyang all abandoned their posts and fled.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，遣使請和於隋，歸其胡墅。

translations.literal: On wuchen envoys were sent to sue for peace with Sui and to return its Hu estates.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Chen sent envoys to sue for peace with Sui and restore the Hu estates.

sentences.zh: 5己巳，立妃沈氏為皇后。

translations.literal: 5 On jisi the consort of the Shen clan was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: 5 On jisi Consort Shen was made empress.

sentences.zh: 辛未，立皇弟叔儼為尋陽王，叔慎為岳陽王，叔達為義陽王，叔能為巴山王，叔虞為武昌王。

translations.literal: On xinwei the emperor's younger brothers Shuyan were made Prince of Xunyang, Shushen Prince of Yueyang, Shuda Prince of Yiyang, Shuneng Prince of Bashan, and Shuyu Prince of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei his brothers Shuyan, Shushen, Shuda, Shuneng, and Shuyu were made princes of Xunyang, Yueyang, Yiyang, Bashan, and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 隋高熲奏，禮不伐喪；

translations.literal: Gao Jiong of Sui memorialized that ritual forbids attacking a state in mourning;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong of Sui argued that ritual forbids attacking a state in mourning;

sentences.zh: 二月，己丑，隋主詔熲等班師。

translations.literal: in the second month, on jichou, the Sui ruler ordered Gao Jiong and the others to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: in the second month, on jichou, the Sui emperor ordered Gao Jiong and the army to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 6三月，己巳，以尚書左僕射晉安王伯恭為湘州刺史，永陽王伯智為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: 6 In the third month, on jisi, Prince of Jin'an Bogong was made governor of Xiang Prefecture, and Prince of Yongyang Bozhi was made Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: 6 On jisi of the third month Prince of Jin'an Bogong became governor of Xiang and Prince of Yongyang Bozhi Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 7夏，四月，庚寅，隋大將軍韓僧壽破突厥於雞頭山，上柱國李充破突厥於河北山。

translations.literal: 7 In summer, the fourth month, on gengyin, the great general of Sui Han Shoushou defeated the Turks at Mount Jitou, and the pillar of state Li Chong defeated the Turks at Mount Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: 7 In summer, on gengyin of the fourth month, Sui general Han Shoushou routed the Turks at Mount Jitou and pillar Li Chong defeated them at Mount Hebei.

sentences.zh: 8丙申，立皇子永康公胤為太子。

translations.literal: 8 On bingshen the emperor's son, the Duke of Yongkang Yin, was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: 8 On bingshen Prince Yongkang Yin was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 胤，孫姬之子也，沈后養以為子。

translations.literal: Yin was the son of Consort Sun; Empress Shen raised him as her own son.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was Consort Sun's child, whom Empress Shen had adopted as her own.

sentences.zh: 9五月，己未，高寶寧引突厥寇隋平州，突厥悉發五可汗控弦之士四十萬入長城。

translations.literal: 9 In the fifth month, on jiwei, Gao Baoning led the Turks to raid Sui's Ping Prefecture; the Turks mustered bowmen from all five qaghans—four hundred thousand entered the Great Wall.
translations.idiomatic: 9 On jiwei of the fifth month Gao Baoning led Turks against Ping; the khans mustered four hundred thousand archers through the Great Wall.

sentences.zh: 10壬戌，隋任穆公于翼卒。

translations.literal: 10 On renxu Duke Mu of Ren, Yu Yi of Sui, died.
translations.idiomatic: 10 On renxu Duke Mu of Ren, Yu Yi of Sui, died.

sentences.zh: 11甲子，隋更命傳國璽曰「受命璽」。

translations.literal: 11 On jiazi Sui renamed the imperial seal of transmission "Seal of Receiving the Mandate."
translations.idiomatic: 11 On jiazi Sui renamed the imperial transmission seal the "Seal of Receiving the Mandate."

sentences.zh: 12六月，甲申，隋遣使來吊。

translations.literal: 12 In the sixth month, on jiashen, Sui sent envoys to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: 12 On jiashen of the sixth month Sui sent envoys of condolence.

sentences.zh: 13乙酉，隋上柱國李光敗突厥於馬邑。

translations.literal: 13 On yiyou the pillar of state Li Guang defeated the Turks at Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: 13 On yiyou pillar Li Guang defeated the Turks at Mayi.

sentences.zh: 突厥又寇蘭州，涼州總管賀婁子干敗之於可洛峐。

translations.literal: The Turks again raided Lan Prefecture; He Luzi'gan, commander of Liang Prefecture, defeated them at Keluoqi.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Lan again; Liang commander He Luzi'gan beat them at Keluoqi.

sentences.zh: 14隋主嫌長安城制度狹小，又宮內多妖異。

translations.literal: 14 The Sui ruler disliked Chang'an's cramped layout and also that within the palace there were many uncanny occurrences.
translations.idiomatic: 14 The Sui emperor found Chang'an cramped and the palace haunted by strange portents.

sentences.zh: 納言蘇威勸帝遷都，帝以初受命，難之；

translations.literal: Counselor Su Wei urged the emperor to move the capital; the emperor, having just received the mandate, found it difficult;
translations.idiomatic: Counselor Su Wei urged relocation, but the newly enthroned emperor hesitated;

sentences.zh: 夜，與威及高熲共議。

translations.literal: at night he discussed it together with Wei and Gao Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: that night he debated the matter with Wei and Gao Jiong.

sentences.zh: 明旦，通直散騎庾季才奏曰：「臣仰觀乾象，俯察圖記，必有遷都之事。

translations.literal: At dawn, the Palace Attendant and Regular Cavalry Yu Jicai memorialized, saying: "Your servant looks up to observe the celestial signs and looks down to examine the charts and records—there must be an affair of moving the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Attendant Yu Jicai memorialized: "I have read heaven above and the charts below—relocation is ordained.

sentences.zh: 且漢營此城，將八百歲，水皆鹹鹵，不甚宜人。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the Han built this city it will be eight hundred years; the water is all brackish and not very fit for people.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founded this city nearly eight hundred years ago; its water is brackish and unwholesome.

sentences.zh: 願陛下協天人之心，為遷徙之計。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to harmonize the hearts of Heaven and man and make plans for migration.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to align heaven and man and plan the move.

sentences.zh: 」帝愕然，謂熲、威曰：「是何神也！

translations.literal: The emperor was startled and said to Jiong and Wei: "What kind of spirit is this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started and exclaimed to Jiong and Wei: "What god sent this man!"

sentences.zh: 」太師李穆亦上表請遷都。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Li Mu also submitted a memorial requesting relocation of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Li Mu also petitioned for relocation.

sentences.zh: 帝省表曰：「天道聰明，已有征應；

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and said: "Heaven's Way is discerning—there are already signs and responses;
translations.idiomatic: Reading the memorials he said: "Heaven has already shown signs;

sentences.zh: 太師人望，復抗此請；

translations.literal: the Grand Preceptor commands men's esteem and again presses this request;
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Preceptor, whom all men respect, presses the same plea;

sentences.zh: 無不可矣。

translations.literal: nothing is impossible now."
translations.idiomatic: nothing more can be refused."

sentences.zh: 」丙申，詔高熲等創造新都於龍首山。

translations.literal: On bingshen he ordered Gao Jiong and the others to create a new capital on Mount Longshou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen he ordered Gao Jiong and others to build a new capital on Mount Longshou.

sentences.zh: 以太子左庶子宇文愷有巧思，領營新都副監。

translations.literal: Because the Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Yu Kai had ingenious ideas, he was put in charge as deputy overseer of building the new capital.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Yu Kai, famed for ingenuity, was made deputy overseer of construction.

sentences.zh: 愷，忻之弟也。

translations.literal: Kai was the younger brother of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai was the younger brother of Xin.

sentences.zh: 15秋，七月，辛未，大赦。

translations.literal: 15 In autumn, the seventh month, on xinwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: 15 In autumn, on xinwei of the seventh month, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙午，設無礙大會於太極殿，捨身及乘輿御服。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingwu, an Unimpeded Assembly was held in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; the emperor offered his body and imperial carriage and robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingwu, an Unimpeded Assembly was held in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; the emperor offered his person and imperial regalia.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty followed.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以長沙王叔堅為司空，將軍、刺史如故。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Prince of Changsha Shujian was made Minister of Works, his generalship and governorship remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Prince of Changsha Shujian was made Minister of Works while keeping his military posts.

sentences.zh: 16冬，十月，癸酉，隋太子勇屯兵咸陽以備突厥。

translations.literal: 16 In winter, the tenth month, on guiyou, the Sui crown prince Yong stationed troops at Xianyang to guard against the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: 16 In winter, on guiyou of the tenth month, Sui crown prince Yong encamped at Xianyang against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 17十二月，丙子，隋命新都曰大興城。

translations.literal: 17 In the twelfth month, on bingzi, Sui named the new capital Daxing City.
translations.idiomatic: 17 On bingzi of the twelfth month Sui named the new capital Daxing City.

sentences.zh: 18乙酉，隋遣沁源公虞慶則屯弘化以備突厥。

translations.literal: 18 On yiyou Sui sent Duke of Qinyuan Yu Qingze to encamp at Honghua to guard against the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: 18 On yiyou Sui sent Duke of Qinyuan Yu Qingze to Honghua against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 行軍總管達奚長儒將兵二千，與突厥沙缽略可汗遇於周槃，沙缽略有眾十餘萬，軍中大懼。

translations.literal: The campaign commander Daxi Changru led two thousand troops and encountered the Türk qaghan Shaboluo at Zhoupan; Shaboluo had a host of more than a hundred thousand, and within the army fear was great.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign commander Daxi Changru with two thousand men met Türk qaghan Shaboluo at Zhoupan; Shaboluo had more than a hundred thousand warriors, and his troops were terrified.

sentences.zh: 長儒神色慷慨，且戰且行，為虜所衝突，散而復聚，四面抗拒。

translations.literal: Changru's expression was ardent; he fought as he marched; though struck and scattered by the enemy, he gathered again and resisted on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Changru's bearing was defiant; he fought as he marched; though broken and scattered, he re-formed and held on every side.

sentences.zh: 轉斗三日，晝夜凡十四戰，五兵鹹盡。

translations.literal: He turned and battled for three days; by day and night there were fourteen engagements in all; the five weapons were all exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: For three days and fourteen battles by day and night every weapon was spent.

sentences.zh: 士卒以拳毆之，手皆骨見，殺傷萬計。

translations.literal: The soldiers beat the foe with their fists; hands showed bone; those killed and wounded numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: His men punched the enemy bare-handed until bone showed through skin; tens of thousands fell on both sides.

sentences.zh: 虜氣稍奪，於是解去。

translations.literal: The enemy's spirit was somewhat taken; thereupon they broke off and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks' ardor finally broke, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 長儒身被五瘡，通中者二；

translations.literal: Changru's body bore five wounds, two of them through-piercing;
translations.idiomatic: Changru took five wounds, two of them through-and-through;

sentences.zh: 其戰士死傷者什八九。

translations.literal: Of his warriors, eight or nine in ten were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly eight or nine soldiers in ten among his troops were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 詔以長儒為上柱國，餘勳回授一子。

translations.literal: An edict made Changru a pillar of state, with the remainder of his merit transferred to ennoble one son.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named Changru a pillar of state and transferred the surplus of his honors to ennoble one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 時柱國馮昱屯乙弗泊，蘭州總管叱列長叉守臨洮，上柱國李崇屯幽州，皆為突厥所敗。

translations.literal: At that time the pillar Feng Yu was encamped at Yifu Marsh, the Lanzhou commander Chilie Changcha guarded Lintao, and the pillar Li Chong was encamped at Youzhou—all were defeated by the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar Feng Yu held Yifu Marsh, Lanzhou commander Chilie Changcha defended Lintao, and pillar Li Chong held Youzhou; the Turks defeated them all.

sentences.zh: 於是突厥縱兵自木硤、石門兩道入寇，武威、天水、安定、金城、上郡、弘化、延安，六畜鹹盡。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Turks released their troops to raid by the two routes of Muxia and Shimen; at Wuwei, Tianshui, Anding, Jincheng, Shang Commandery, Honghua, and Yan'an, the six kinds of livestock were all exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks then poured through Muxia and Shimen, stripping Wuwei, Tianshui, Anding, Jincheng, Shang, Honghua, and Yan'an of all livestock.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略更欲南入，達頭不從，引兵而去。

translations.literal: Shaboluo further wished to advance south; Datou did not consent and led his troops away.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo wanted to push farther south, but Datou refused and withdrew with his forces.

sentences.zh: 長孫晟又說沙缽略之子染干詐告沙缽略曰：「鐵勒等反，欲襲其牙。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Sheng again persuaded Shaboluo's son Ran'gan to feign report to Shaboluo, saying: "The Tiele and others have rebelled and wish to strike his royal camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Sheng also induced Shaboluo's son Ran'gan to send a false report: "The Tiele have risen and mean to strike your royal camp."

sentences.zh: 」沙缽略懼，回兵出塞。

translations.literal: " Shaboluo was afraid and turned his army back out of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Shaboluo wheeled his army back beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 19隋主既立，待遇梁主，恩禮彌厚。

translations.literal: 19 Once the Sui ruler had been established, his treatment of the Liang ruler grew ever more generous in favor and ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: 19 After his accession the Sui emperor treated the Liang sovereign with ever greater favor and ceremony.

sentences.zh: 是歲，納梁主女為晉王妃，又欲以其子瑒尚蘭陵公主。

translations.literal: That year he took the Liang ruler's daughter as consort to the Prince of Jin and also wished to marry his son Yang to Princess Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: That year he took a daughter of the Liang ruler as consort of the Prince of Jin and proposed that his son Yang marry Princess Lanling.

sentences.zh: 由是罷江陵總管，梁主始得專制其國。

translations.literal: Thereby the Jiangling area commander was abolished, and the Liang ruler was able at last to exercise sole rule over his state.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangling garrison command was abolished, and the Liang ruler at last governed his realm without interference.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，庚子，隋將入新都，大赦。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, on gengzi, as Sui was about to enter the new capital, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, on gengzi of the first month, with Sui about to move into the new capital, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 2壬寅，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: 2 On renyin, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: 2 On renyin Sui proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 初，上病創，不能視事，政無大小，皆決於長沙王叔堅，權傾朝廷。

translations.literal: At the beginning the emperor was wounded and could not attend to affairs; great and small in government were all decided by Prince of Changsha Shujian, whose power tilted the court.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor convalesced from his wounds and could not govern, Prince Shujian of Changsha decided every affair of state and dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 叔堅頗驕縱，上由是忌之。

translations.literal: Shujian was rather arrogant and unrestrained; the emperor therefore came to dislike him.
translations.idiomatic: Shujian grew arrogant and unrestrained, and the emperor came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 都官尚書山陰孔范，中書舍人施文慶，皆惡叔堅而有寵於上，日夕求其短，構之於上。

translations.literal: Kong Fan of Shanyin, Director of the Department of Justice, and Shi Wenqing, Attendant of the Secretariat, both hated Shujian yet enjoyed favor with the emperor; day and night they sought his faults and set traps for him before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Justice Kong Fan of Shanyin and Secretariat Attendant Shi Wenqing, both favored at court and hostile to Shujian, spent every hour hunting for flaws to denounce him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上乃即叔堅驃騎將軍本號，用三司之儀，出為江州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor then restored Shujian to his original title of General of Agile Cavalry but with the ceremonies of the Three Excellencies, and sent him out as governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor retained Shujian's title of General of Agile Cavalry but granted him Three Excellency ceremonies before posting him to Jiangzhou as governor.

sentences.zh: 以祠部尚書江總為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Jiang Zong, Director of the Department of Ritual, was made Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zong, Director of the Department of Ritual, was made Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，立皇子深為始安王。

translations.literal: On guimao the emperor's son Shen was established as Prince of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Prince Shen was enfeoffed as Prince of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 3二月，己巳朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: 3 In the second month, on the first day jisi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: 3 On the first of jisi in the second month there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 4癸酉，遣兼散騎常侍賀徹等聘於隋。

translations.literal: 4 On guiyou the court sent the concurrent Regular Attendant of the Secretariat He Che and others on a mission of courtesy to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: 4 On guiyou Chen sent He Che, Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Secretariat, and others on a diplomatic mission to Sui.

sentences.zh: 5突厥寇隋北邊。

translations.literal: 5 The Turks raided Sui's northern border.
translations.idiomatic: 5 The Turks raided Sui's northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 6癸巳，葬孝宣皇帝顯寧陵，廟號高宗。

translations.literal: 6 On guisi the Xiao Xuan Emperor was buried at Xianning Mausoleum, with the temple name Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: 6 On guisi Emperor Xiao Xuan was interred at Xianning Mausoleum with the temple name Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 7右衛將軍兼中書通事舍人司馬申既掌機密，頗作威福，多所譖毀。

translations.literal: 7 The Right Guard General and concurrent Attendant for Palace Communications Sima Shen, having grasped confidential affairs, greatly wielded power and favor and widely slandered others.
translations.idiomatic: 7 Sima Shen, Right Guard General and concurrent Attendant for Palace Communications, held the emperor's confidence and abused his power, slandering many at court.

sentences.zh: 能候人主顏色，有忤己者，必以微言譖之；

translations.literal: He could watch the sovereign's expression; those who offended him he was sure to slander with subtle words;
translations.idiomatic: He read the emperor's mood; anyone who crossed him was quietly denounced;

sentences.zh: 附已者，因機進之。

translations.literal: those who attached to him he advanced by seizing opportune moments.
translations.idiomatic: those who curried his favor he promoted at the first opportunity.

sentences.zh: 是以朝廷內外，皆從風而靡。

translations.literal: Therefore within and without the court, all bent before the wind.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court, inside and out, bowed to his influence.

sentences.zh: 上欲用侍中、吏部尚書毛喜為僕射，申惡喜強直，言於上曰：「喜，臣之妻兄，高宗時稱陛下有酒德，請逐去宮臣，陛下寧忘之邪？

translations.literal: The emperor wished to appoint the Palace Attendant and Director of the Department of State Affairs Mao Xi as Vice Director; Shen hated Xi's firm uprightness and said to the emperor: "Xi is my wife's elder brother. In the time of Gaozong he said Your Majesty had the virtue of wine and asked that palace ministers be driven away—does Your Majesty not still remember?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor meant to make Palace Attendant Mao Xi Vice Director, Shen, who loathed Xi's blunt integrity, reminded him: "Xi is my brother-in-law. In Gaozong's day he praised your taste for wine and urged you to dismiss the palace staff—have you forgotten?"

sentences.zh: 」上乃止。

translations.literal: " The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor dropped the appointment.

sentences.zh: 上創愈，置酒於後殿以自慶，引吏部尚書江總以下展樂賦詩。

translations.literal: When the emperor's wounds had healed, he set out wine in the rear hall to celebrate, summoning Jiang Zong, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and those below for music and poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Once recovered, the emperor held a celebratory banquet in the rear hall and summoned Jiang Zong and the other ministers for music and verse.

sentences.zh: 既醉而命毛喜。

translations.literal: When he was drunk he summoned Mao Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he sent for Mao Xi.

sentences.zh: 於時山陵初畢，喜見之，不懌；

translations.literal: At that time the imperial tomb ritual had just been completed; when Xi saw it, he was displeased;
translations.idiomatic: The imperial mourning had only just ended, and Xi was dismayed;

sentences.zh: 欲諫，則上已醉。

translations.literal: he wished to remonstrate, but the emperor was already drunk.
translations.idiomatic: he wanted to remonstrate, but the emperor was already drunk.

sentences.zh: 喜升階，陽為心疾，僕於階下，移出省中。

translations.literal: Xi ascended the steps, pretended a heart ailment, and collapsed at the foot of the steps; he was moved out of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xi climbed the steps, feigned a heart seizure, and collapsed; attendants carried him out of the ministry compound.

sentences.zh: 上醒，謂江總曰：「我悔召毛喜，彼實無疾，但欲阻我歡宴，非我所為耳。

translations.literal: When the emperor sobered he said to Jiang Zong: "I regret summoning Mao Xi. He truly had no illness—he only wished to block my merry feast; that is not what I would have had done.
translations.idiomatic: When he sobered the emperor told Jiang Zong, "I regret sending for Mao Xi. He wasn't ill—he only wanted to spoil my feast. That was presumptuous of him."

sentences.zh: 」乃與司馬申謀曰：「此人負氣，吾欲乞鄱陽兄弟，聽其報仇，可乎？

translations.literal: " He then plotted with Sima Shen, saying: "This man is proud-spirited. I wish to beg the brothers of Poyang and let them take revenge—is that possible?
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Sima Shen, "This man is proud. What if I give the Poyang brothers leave to take revenge on him?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「彼終不為官用，願如聖旨。

translations.literal: " He replied: "He will never serve in office in the end. I wish it as Your Majesty commands.
translations.idiomatic: " "He would never truly serve you anyway," Shen answered. "Let it be as Your Majesty wishes."

sentences.zh: 」中書通事舍人北地傅縡爭之曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Fu Zai of Beidi, Attendant for Palace Communications, argued against it, saying: "That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Zai of Beidi, Attendant for Palace Communications, objected: "No."

sentences.zh: 若許報仇，欲置先皇何地？

translations.literal: If revenge is permitted, where is the late emperor to be placed?
translations.idiomatic: If you allow private revenge, what becomes of your father's dignity?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「當乞一小郡，勿令見人事耳。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "We should grant him a small commandery and not let him witness court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Give him some minor prefecture and keep him away from court."

sentences.zh: 」乃以喜為永嘉內史。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xi was made Interior Secretary of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: " Mao Xi was made Interior Secretary of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 8三月，丙辰，隋遷於新都。

translations.literal: 8 In the third month, on bingchen, Sui moved to the new capital.
translations.idiomatic: 8 On bingchen of the third month Sui moved into the new capital.

sentences.zh: 初令民二十一成丁，減役者每歲十二番為二十日役，減調絹一匹為二丈。

translations.literal: For the first time the people were told that at twenty-one one became an adult; for those whose labor service was reduced, each year's twelve rotations became twenty days of service, and the silk tribute of one bolt per levy was reduced to two zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Adults were defined at twenty-one; corvée was cut from twelve tours a year to twenty days, and the silk levy from one full bolt to two zhang.

sentences.zh: 週末榷酒坊、鹽池、鹽井，至是皆罷之。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhou monopolies were placed on wine shops, salt ponds, and salt wells; by this time all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's monopolies on breweries, salt pans, and brine wells were abolished.

sentences.zh: 秘書監牛弘上表，以「典籍屢經喪亂，率多散逸。

translations.literal: Secretary Director Niu Hong submitted a memorial, stating: "The classics have repeatedly suffered turmoil and loss; for the most part they have scattered and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Director Niu Hong memorialized: "Classics have been lost again and again in the upheavals, and most copies have scattered and vanished."

sentences.zh: 周氏聚書，僅盈萬卷。

translations.literal: The Zhou house gathered books, barely filling ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou court had assembled barely ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 平齊所得，除其重雜，裁益五千。

translations.literal: From the conquest of Qi, after removing the heavy and miscellaneous, there was an increase of only five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The conquest of Qi added only five thousand after duplicates were culled.

sentences.zh: 興集之期，屬膺聖世。

translations.literal: The time to gather and restore them falls under a sage age.
translations.idiomatic: The moment to gather them has come under a sage reign.

sentences.zh: 為國之本，莫此為先。

translations.literal: For the foundation of the state, nothing comes before this.
translations.idiomatic: For the foundation of the state, nothing comes before this.

sentences.zh: 豈可使之流落私家，不歸王府！

translations.literal: How can they be allowed to drift into private homes and not return to the royal repository!
translations.idiomatic: How can we let them drift into private hands and never return to the imperial library!

sentences.zh: 必須勒之以天威，引之以微利，則異典必臻，觀閣斯積。

translations.literal: One must compel them with imperial majesty and entice them with small profit, and then rare classics will surely arrive and the viewing halls will thus be filled.
translations.idiomatic: We must enforce this with imperial authority and reward it with modest profit, and rare texts will surely come in until the palace libraries are full again.

sentences.zh: 」隋主從之。

translations.literal: " The Sui ruler followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Sui emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，詔購求遺書於天下，每獻書一卷，賚縑一匹。

translations.literal: On dingsi an edict sought lost books throughout the realm; for each scroll presented one bolt of silk was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi an edict sought lost books throughout the realm; one bolt of silk was paid for each scroll presented.

sentences.zh: 9夏，四月，庚午，吐谷渾寇隋臨洮。

translations.literal: 9 In summer, the fourth month, on gengwu, the Tuyuhun raided Sui's Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: 9 On gengwu in the fourth month the Tuyuhun raided Lintao.

sentences.zh: 洮州刺史皮子信出戰，敗死；

translations.literal: The prefect of Tao Pi Zixin went out to battle and was defeated and killed;
translations.idiomatic: Tao prefect Pi Zixin marched out to fight and was killed in defeat;

sentences.zh: 汶州總管梁遠擊走之。

translations.literal: the Wenzhou commander Liang Yuan struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhou commander Liang Yuan drove them back.

sentences.zh: 又寇廓州，州兵擊走之。

translations.literal: They again raided Zuo Prefecture; the prefectural troops struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Zuo Prefecture next and were beaten back by local troops.

sentences.zh: 10壬申，隋以尚書右僕射趙煚兼內史令。

translations.literal: 10 On renshen Sui made Vice Director Zhao Jiong also Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: 10 On renshen Sui made Vice Director Zhao Jiong also Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 11突厥數為隋寇。

translations.literal: 11 The Turks repeatedly raided Sui.
translations.idiomatic: 11 The Turks raided Sui again and again.

sentences.zh: 隋主下詔曰：「往者周、齊抗衡，分割諸夏，突厥之虜，俱通二國。

translations.literal: The Sui ruler issued an edict, saying: "Formerly Zhou and Qi contended in strength, dividing the Central Lands; the Türk barbarians maintained relations with both states.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor issued an edict: "Once Zhou and Qi stood opposed and split the realm; the Türks dealt with both alike."

sentences.zh: 周人東慮，恐齊好之深，齊氏西慮，懼周交之厚；

translations.literal: The Zhou people worried in the east, fearing Qi's ties were deep; the Qi house worried in the west, dreading Zhou's friendship was thick;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou feared Qi was courting them too warmly in the east; Qi feared Zhou was doing the same in the west;

sentences.zh: 謂虜意輕重，國遂安危，蓋並有大敵之憂，思減一邊之防也。

translations.literal: they believed the barbarians' favor weighed heavy or light and the states were thus secure or endangered—both alike had the anxiety of a great foe and sought to lessen defenses on one flank.
translations.idiomatic: each thought the Türks' goodwill decided its survival, for both dreaded a powerful neighbor and hoped to ease one frontier by bribing the steppe.

sentences.zh: 朕以為厚斂兆庶，多惠豺狼，未嘗感恩，資而為賊。

translations.literal: I hold that heavily taxing the multitude to lavish favors on wolves and jackals—they never felt gratitude and instead used our gifts to become raiders.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that taxing the people heavily to enrich wolves and jackals wins no gratitude—they take our gifts and raid us all the same.

sentences.zh: 節之以禮，不為虛費，省徭薄賦，國用有餘。

translations.literal: Restraint through ritual, no empty expenditure; reducing corvée and lightening levies—the national treasury has surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Govern by ritual, spend nothing in vain, lighten corvée and reduce levies, and the treasury will have surplus.

sentences.zh: 因入賊之物，加賜將士；

translations.literal: with goods taken from the raiders, bonus rewards for officers and soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Reward the troops from what we seize from the raiders;

sentences.zh: 息道路之民，務為耕織；

translations.literal: giving rest to the people of the roads, devoting themselves to plowing and weaving;
translations.idiomatic: let the people on the roads return home to plow and weave;

sentences.zh: 清邊制勝，成策在心。

translations.literal: securing the frontier and mastering victory—the completed strategy lies in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: secure the borders and win—the plan is already complete in my mind.

sentences.zh: 凶丑愚闇，未知深旨，將大定之日，比戰國之時；

translations.literal: The vicious and ugly, stupid and dark, do not know its deep intent; on the eve of great pacification they compare it to Warring States times;
translations.idiomatic: These brutish fools do not grasp my purpose; on the eve of universal peace they behave as if we were back in the Warring States;

sentences.zh: 乘昔世之驕，結今時之恨。

translations.literal: riding the arrogance of former ages, they forge present resentments.
translations.idiomatic: they ride old arrogance and nurse new hatred.

sentences.zh: 近者盡其巢窟，俱犯北邊，蓋上天所忿，驅就齊斧。

translations.literal: Recently they emptied their nests and dens, all invading the northern border—this is surely Heaven's wrath, driving them toward the executioner's axe.
translations.idiomatic: Lately they have emptied their nests and poured against the north—Heaven itself is angry and driving them to the headsman's block.

sentences.zh: 諸將今行，義兼含育，有降者納，有違者死，使其不敢南望，永服威刑。

translations.literal: The generals going forth now combine righteousness with cherishing and nurturing: those who submit will be received, those who resist will die, so that they dare not look south and forever submit to awe-inspiring punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The generals I send now will temper force with mercy: receive those who surrender, kill those who resist, until they dare not look south again and forever bow to our might.

sentences.zh: 何用侍子之朝，寧勞渭橋之拜！

translations.literal: Why need the morning audience of a hostage prince, or trouble the bowing at Wei Bridge!
translations.idiomatic: Why should I wait for a hostage prince at court, or trouble myself with a bow at Wei Bridge!

sentences.zh: 於是命衛王爽等為行軍元帥，分八道出塞擊之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Prince Wei Shuang and others as campaign marshals, dividing into eight routes to go beyond the passes and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Prince Wei Shuang and others campaign marshals and sent eight columns beyond the passes to strike them.

sentences.zh: 爽督總管李充等四將出朔州道，己卯，與沙缽略可汗遇於白道。

translations.literal: Shuang supervised the area commanders Li Chong and four other generals on the Shuozhou route; on jimao they encountered the Türk qaghan Shaboluo at White Route.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang led area commanders Li Chong and three other generals on the Shuozhou route; on jimao they met Türk qaghan Shaboluo at White Route.

sentences.zh: 李充言於爽曰：「突厥狃於驟勝，必輕我而無備。

translations.literal: Li Chong said to Shuang: "The Turks, accustomed to sudden victories, are sure to despise us and be unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong told Shuang, "The Turks, flushed with easy victories, will surely despise us and leave themselves unguarded."

sentences.zh: 以精兵襲之，可破也。

translations.literal: With elite troops make a surprise attack on them—it can be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Strike them with picked troops and you can break them."

sentences.zh: 」諸將多以為疑，唯長史李徹贊成之，遂與充帥精騎五千掩擊突厥，大破之。

translations.literal: " Most generals doubted, but only the chief aide Li Che approved it; thereupon with Chong he led five thousand elite horsemen in a concealed strike on the Turks and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: " Most of the generals were skeptical, but chief aide Li Che agreed; he and Chong then led five thousand picked horsemen in a surprise attack and routed the Turks.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略棄所服金甲，潛草中而遁。

translations.literal: Shaboluo cast off the golden armor he wore and fled hidden in the grass.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo stripped off his golden armor and crawled away through the grass.

sentences.zh: 其軍中無食，粉骨為糧，加以疾疫，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: His army had no food; they ground bone into rations; moreover pestilence—those who died were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: His army ran out of food and ground bone into meal; pestilence followed, and the dead were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 幽州總管陰壽帥步騎十萬出盧龍塞，擊高寶寧。

translations.literal: Youzhou commander Yin Shou led infantry and cavalry one hundred thousand out through Lulong Pass to attack Gao Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou commander Yin Shou led a hundred thousand foot and horse out through Lulong Pass against Gao Baoning.

sentences.zh: 寶寧求救於突厥，突厥方御隋師，不能救。

translations.literal: Baoning begged the Türks for rescue; the Türks were then resisting Sui troops and could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: Baoning begged the Türks for help, but they were fully engaged against Sui and could not come.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，寶寧棄城奔磧北，和龍諸縣悉平。

translations.literal: On gengchen Baoning abandoned the city and fled north of the sands; all counties of Helong were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Baoning abandoned his city and fled north of the desert; the Helong counties were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 壽設重賞以購寶寧，又遣人離其腹心；

translations.literal: Shou set heavy rewards to hunt Baoning and also sent men to alienate his inner circle;
translations.idiomatic: Yin Shou offered heavy rewards for Baoning's head and sent agents to turn his followers against him;

sentences.zh: 寶寧奔契丹，為其麾下所殺。

translations.literal: Baoning fled to the Khitan and was killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Baoning fled to the Khitan and was killed by his own men.

sentences.zh: 12己丑，郢州城主張子譏遣使請降於隋，隋主以和好，不納。

translations.literal: 12 On jichou the Yingzhou fortress commander Zhang Ziji sent envoys to request surrender to Sui; the Sui ruler, for sake of good relations, did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: 12 On jichou Yingzhou commander Zhang Ziji sent envoys offering surrender to Sui; the Sui emperor, honoring the peace, refused.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，隋主遣兼散騎常侍薛舒、兼散騎常侍王劭來聘。

translations.literal: On xinmao the Sui ruler sent the concurrent Regular Attendants Xue Shu and Wang Shao on a mission of courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the Sui emperor sent Concurrent Regular Attendants Xue Shu and Wang Shao on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 劭，松年之子也。

translations.literal: Shao was the son of Songnian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao was the son of Songnian.

sentences.zh: 13癸巳，隋主大雩。

translations.literal: 13 On guisi the Sui ruler performed a grand rain prayer.
translations.idiomatic: 13 On guisi the Sui emperor performed a grand rain prayer.

sentences.zh: 14甲子，突厥遣使入見於隋。

translations.literal: 14 On jiazi Türks sent envoys to appear at audience in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: 14 On jiazi the Türks sent envoys to audience at Sui.

sentences.zh: 15隋改度支尚書為民部，都官尚書為刑部。

translations.literal: 15 Sui changed Director of Revenue to Director of the People and Director of Justice to Director of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: 15 Sui renamed the Director of Revenue the Director of the People and the Director of Justice the Director of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 命左僕射判吏、禮、兵三部事，右僕射判民、刑、工三部事。

translations.literal: The Left Vice Director was ordered to oversee Personnel, Rites, and War; the Right Vice Director the People, Punishments, and Works.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Vice Director was to oversee Personnel, Rites, and War; the Right Vice Director the People, Punishments, and Works.

sentences.zh: 廢光祿、衛尉、鴻臚寺及都水台。

translations.literal: The Directorates of the Imperial Household, Palace Guard, Reception, and the Directorate of Waterways were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorates of the Imperial Household, Palace Guard, Reception, and Waterways were abolished.

sentences.zh: 16五月，癸卯，隋行軍總管李晃破突厥於摩那度口。

translations.literal: 16 In the fifth month, on guimao, Sui campaign commander Li Huang defeated the Turks at Monadu Ford.
translations.idiomatic: 16 On guimao of the fifth month Sui campaign commander Li Huang defeated the Turks at Monadu Ford.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，梁太子琮入朝於隋，賀遷都。

translations.literal: On yisi the Liang crown prince Cong entered audience at Sui to congratulate the move of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Liang crown prince Cong came to Sui to congratulate the move of the capital.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，隋主祀方澤。

translations.literal: On xinyou the Sui ruler sacrificed at the Square Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the Sui emperor sacrificed at the Square Mound.

sentences.zh: 隋秦州總管竇榮定帥九總管步騎三萬出涼州，與突厥阿波可汗相拒於高越原，阿波屢敗。

translations.literal: Sui's Qinzhou commander Dou Rongding led the nine area commanders with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry out from Liangzhou; they faced the Türk qaghan Apo at Gaoyue Plain; Apo was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's Qinzhou commander Dou Rongding led thirty thousand foot and horse from nine area commanders out of Liangzhou and faced Türk qaghan Apo at Gaoyue Plain; Apo was beaten again and again.

sentences.zh: 榮定，熾之兄子也。

translations.literal: Rongding was the elder brother's son of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Rongding was the nephew of Chi.

sentences.zh: 前上大將軍京兆史萬歲，坐事配敦煌為戍卒，詣榮定軍門，請自效。

translations.literal: The former Senior General Shi Wansui of Jingzhao, punished for an offense and assigned to Dunhuang as a garrison soldier, came to Rongding's camp gate requesting to offer his service.
translations.idiomatic: Former Senior General Shi Wansui of Jingzhao, banished to Dunhuang as a garrison soldier for a crime, came to Rongding's camp and asked to serve.

sentences.zh: 榮定素聞其名，見而大悅。

translations.literal: Rongding had long heard his name; on seeing him he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Rongding had long heard of him and was delighted when they met.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，將戰，榮定遣人謂突厥曰：「士卒何罪而殺之！

translations.literal: On renxu, about to give battle, Rongding sent someone to say to the Turks: "What crime have the soldiers committed that you kill them!
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, as battle was about to begin, Rongding sent word to the Turks: "What crime have your soldiers committed that you must slaughter them!

sentences.zh: 但當各遣一壯土決勝負耳。

translations.literal: Only let each side send one stalwart warrior to decide victory or defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Let each side send a single champion to settle the outcome.

sentences.zh: 」突厥許諾，因遣一騎挑戰。

translations.literal: " The Türks agreed and sent one rider to challenge.
translations.idiomatic: " The Türks agreed and sent a lone horseman to issue the challenge.

sentences.zh: 榮定遣萬歲出應之，萬歲馳斬其首而還。

translations.literal: Rongding sent Wansui out to meet him; Wansui galloped forth, cut off his head, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Rongding sent Wansui to answer the challenge; Wansui charged out, struck off the man's head, and rode back.

sentences.zh: 突厥大驚，不敢復戰，遂請盟，引軍而去。

translations.literal: The Türks were greatly alarmed, dared not fight again, then asked for peace, and led their army away.
translations.idiomatic: The Türks were shaken, dared not renew the fight, sued for peace, and withdrew their army.

sentences.zh: 長孫晟時在榮定軍中為偏將，使謂阿波曰：「攝圖每來，戰皆大勝。

translations.literal: Changsun Sheng was then a subordinate general in Rongding's army; he had someone tell Apo: "Whenever Shetu comes, his battles are great victories.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Sheng, serving then as a deputy in Rongding's command, sent word to Apo: "Each time Shetu takes the field, he wins a sweeping victory.

sentences.zh: 阿波才入，遽即奔敗，此乃突厥之恥也。

translations.literal: Apo has only just arrived and at once flees in defeat—this is shame for the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: You have barely joined battle and already run—this is a disgrace to the Türk nation.

sentences.zh: 且攝圖之與阿波，兵勢本敵。

translations.literal: Moreover, Shetu and Apo were originally matched in military strength.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, you and Shetu were once evenly matched in force.

sentences.zh: 今攝圖日勝，為眾所崇；

translations.literal: Now Shetu wins day by day and is revered by the masses;
translations.idiomatic: Now Shetu wins victory after victory and is exalted by the tribes;

sentences.zh: 阿波不利，為國生辱。

translations.literal: Apo fares ill and brings shame upon the state.
translations.idiomatic: your setbacks bring dishonor on the realm.

sentences.zh: 攝圖必當以罪歸阿波，成其宿計，滅北牙矣。

translations.literal: Shetu is sure to lay the blame on Apo, fulfill his long-standing design, and destroy the Northern Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Shetu will surely shift the fault onto you, carry out his old scheme, and wipe out the Northern Yamen.

sentences.zh: 願自量度，能御之乎？

translations.literal: I urge you to measure yourself—can you withstand him?"
translations.idiomatic: Measure your own strength: can you stand against him?"

sentences.zh: 」阿波使至，晟又謂之曰：「今達頭與隋連和，而攝圖不能制，可汗何不依附天子，連結達頭，相合為強，此萬全計也，豈若喪兵負罪，歸就攝圖，受其戮辱邪！

translations.literal: " When Apo's envoy arrived, Sheng again told him: "Now Tardu is allied with Sui, yet Shetu cannot control him. Why does the qaghan not attach himself to the Son of Heaven, join with Tardu, and unite your strength—this is a plan without risk. How does that compare with losing troops, bearing guilt, returning to Shetu, and suffering slaughter and humiliation!"
translations.idiomatic: " When Apo's envoy came, Sheng told him again: "Tardu is now at peace with Sui, and Shetu cannot master him. Why not rely on the Son of Heaven, ally with Tardu, and make yourselves strong together? That is the sure course. Would you rather lose your army, bear the blame, go back to Shetu, and face execution and disgrace?"

sentences.zh: 」阿波然之，遣使隨晟入朝。

translations.literal: " Apo thought this right and sent envoys to follow Sheng into court.
translations.idiomatic: " Apo agreed, and sent envoys to accompany Sheng to the Sui court.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略素忌阿波驍悍；

translations.literal: Shabolü had long resented Apo's fierceness and daring;
translations.idiomatic: Shabolü had long envied Apo's martial prowess;

sentences.zh: 自白道敗歸，又聞阿波貳於隋，因先歸，襲擊北牙，大破之，殺阿波之母。

translations.literal: since returning defeated from Baidao he also heard that Apo was disloyal to Sui; he therefore returned first, struck the Northern Yamen, routed it utterly, and killed Apo's mother.
translations.idiomatic: after his defeat on the Baidao road he learned Apo was leaning toward Sui; he hurried home, fell on the Northern Yamen, crushed it, and killed Apo's mother.

sentences.zh: 阿波還，無所歸，西奔達頭。

translations.literal: Apo returned and had nowhere to go; he fled west to Tardu.
translations.idiomatic: Apo came back to find no refuge and fled west to Tardu.

sentences.zh: 達頭大怒，遣阿波帥兵而東，其部落歸之者將十萬騎，遂與沙缽略相攻，屢破之，復得故地，兵勢益強。

translations.literal: Tardu was greatly angered and sent Apo east at the head of troops; tribes that rejoined him amounted to nearly a hundred thousand horse; he then fought Shabolü, repeatedly defeated him, recovered his old lands, and his military power grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Tardu was furious and sent Apo east with an army; clans rallying to him numbered nearly a hundred thousand horse. He fought Shabolü again and again, broke him, regained lost territory, and grew stronger still.

sentences.zh: 貪汗可汗素睦於阿波，沙缽略奪其眾而廢之，貪汗亡奔達頭。

translations.literal: Qaghan Tanhan had long been on good terms with Apo; Shabolü seized his followers and deposed him, and Tanhan fled to join Tardu.
translations.idiomatic: The Greedy Khan Tanhan had been friendly with Apo; Shabolü seized his people and removed him, and Tanhan fled to Tardu.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略從弟地勤察，別統部落，與沙缽略有隙，復以眾叛歸阿波。

translations.literal: Shabolü's younger cousin Di Qincha commanded a separate tribe; he had a rift with Shabolü and again rebelled with his followers to join Apo.
translations.idiomatic: Shabolü's cousin Di Qincha led a separate tribe, quarreled with him, and took his men over to Apo.

sentences.zh: 連兵不已，各遣使詣長安請和求援。

translations.literal: Fighting went on without cease; each side sent envoys to Chang'an to sue for peace and beg aid.
translations.idiomatic: The war did not end; both sides sent envoys to Chang'an seeking peace and support.

sentences.zh: 隋主皆不許。

translations.literal: The Sui ruler refused them all.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor refused every request.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚辰，隋行軍總管梁遠破吐谷渾於爾汗山。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengchen, Sui campaign commander Liang Yuan defeated the Tuyuhun at Mount Erhan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengchen, Sui campaign commander Liang Yuan defeated the Tuyuhun at Mount Erhan.

sentences.zh: 突厥寇幽州，隋幽州總管廣宗壯公李崇帥步騎三千拒之。

translations.literal: The Türks raided Youzhou; Sui Youzhou commander Duke Zhuang of Guangzong, Li Chong, led three thousand foot and horse to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The Türks invaded Youzhou; Sui Youzhou commander Li Chong, Duke Zhuang of Guangzong, led three thousand infantry and cavalry against them.

sentences.zh: 轉戰十餘日，師人多死，遂保砂城。

translations.literal: After more than ten days of fighting back and forth, most of the army had died; they then held Shacheng.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten days they fought on the move until most of the force was dead; they then took refuge in Shacheng.

sentences.zh: 突厥圍之，城荒頹，不可守禦。

translations.literal: The Türks besieged it; the walls were ruined and crumbling and could not be defended.
translations.idiomatic: The Türks surrounded the town; its walls were broken and wasted and could not be held.

sentences.zh: 曉夕力戰，又無所食。

translations.literal: They fought hard from dawn to dusk, yet had nothing to eat.
translations.idiomatic: They battled from dawn to dusk but had no food.

sentences.zh: 每夜出掠虜營，得六畜以繼軍糧。

translations.literal: Each night they sallied to raid the enemy camp and took livestock to supplement army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Each night they slipped out to raid the barbarian camp and seized livestock to feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 突厥畏之，厚為其備，每夜中結陳以待之。

translations.literal: The Türks feared them, made heavy preparations, and every midnight formed battle lines to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The Türks grew wary, strengthened their guard, and every night formed ranks to meet them.

sentences.zh: 崇軍苦饑，出輒遇敵，死亡略盡。

translations.literal: Chong's army suffered bitter hunger; whenever they went out they met the enemy, and deaths were nearly total.
