translations.idiomatic: Chong's men starved; each sortie met the enemy, and they were nearly all killed.

sentences.zh: 及明，奔還城者尚百許人，然多傷重，不更堪戰。

translations.literal: When day broke, barely a hundred who had fled back to the city remained, and most were badly wounded and could fight no more.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn barely a hundred had straggled back inside, most gravely wounded and fit for no further combat.

sentences.zh: 突厥意欲降之，遣使謂崇曰：「若來降者，封為特勒。

translations.literal: The Türks wished to accept his surrender and sent an envoy to tell Chong: "If you come down, you will be enfeoffed as a tele.
translations.idiomatic: The Türks meant to take him alive and sent word: "Surrender, and you shall be made a tele.

sentences.zh: 」崇知不免，令其士卒曰：「崇喪師徒，罪當萬死。

translations.literal: " Knowing he could not escape, Chong told his soldiers: "Chong has lost the army and deserves death ten thousand times over.
translations.idiomatic: " Seeing no escape, Chong told his men: "I have lost the army and deserve ten thousand deaths.

sentences.zh: 今日效命，以謝國家。

translations.literal: Today I give my life to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: Today I will spend my life to repay the realm.

sentences.zh: 汝俟吾死，且可降賊，便散走，努力還鄉。

translations.literal: You wait until I am dead; then you may surrender to the enemy, scatter and flee, and strive to reach home.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until I am dead; then you may yield to the enemy, break up, and make your way home as best you can.

sentences.zh: 若見至尊，道崇此意。

translations.literal: If you see His Majesty, tell him Chong's meaning."
translations.idiomatic: If you see His Majesty, give him my message."

sentences.zh: 」乃挺刃突陳，復殺二人，突厥亂射，殺之。

translations.literal: " He then grasped his blade, charged the line, killed two more men; the Türks shot him in confusion and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " He seized his blade, broke into the enemy ranks, and killed two more; the Türks loosed a volley and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛丑，以豫州刺史代人周搖為幽州總管。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinchou, the man of Dai Zhou Yao was made Youzhou commander.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinchou, Zhou Yao of Dai was appointed Youzhou commander.

sentences.zh: 命李崇子敏襲爵。

translations.literal: He ordered Li Chong's son Min to inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Li Chong's son Min to succeed to the peerage.

sentences.zh: 敏娶樂平公主之女娥英，詔假一品羽儀，禮如尚帝女。

translations.literal: Min married Eying, daughter of Princess Leping; an edict granted him first-rank ceremonial guard, with rites like those for an imperial princess.
translations.idiomatic: Min married Eying, daughter of Princess Leping; an edict gave him first-rank ceremonial escort, with honors like an imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 既而將侍宴，公主謂敏曰：「我以四海與至尊，唯一婿，當為爾求柱國；

translations.literal: When he was soon to attend a banquet, the princess told Min: "I gave the realm to His Majesty for one son-in-law alone; I shall secure a pillar of state for you;
translations.idiomatic: Before a court feast the princess told Min: "I gave my brother the empire—there is only you for a son-in-law; I mean to win you the rank of pillar of state;

sentences.zh: 若余官，汝慎勿謝。

translations.literal: for any other office, be careful not to thank him."
translations.idiomatic: if he offers lesser posts, do not thank him."

sentences.zh: 」及進見，帝授以儀同及開府，皆不謝。

translations.literal: " When he came before the throne, the emperor granted him Companion in Rank and Genesis Chief; he thanked neither.
translations.idiomatic: " At audience the emperor gave him Companion in Rank and Genesis Chief; Min did not bow his thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公主有大功於我，我何得於其婿而惜官乎！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The princess has great merit toward me—how could I be stingy with offices toward her son-in-law!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Your mother-in-law has done me great service—how could I stint her son-in-law on rank!

sentences.zh: 今授汝柱國。

translations.literal: Now I grant you pillar of state."
translations.idiomatic: I now make you pillar of state."

sentences.zh: 」敏乃拜而蹈舞。

translations.literal: Min then bowed and performed the step dance.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Min bow and perform the step dance of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 17八月，丁卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: 17 In the eighth month, on dingmao the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: 17 In the eighth month, on dingmao the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 18長沙王叔堅未之江州，復留為司空，實奪之權。

translations.literal: 18 Prince of Changsha Shujian had not yet gone to Jiangzhou; he was again kept on as Minister of Works, but in fact his power was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: 18 Prince of Changsha Shujian had not yet left for Jiangzhou; he was kept as Minister of Works in name while stripped of real authority.

sentences.zh: 19壬午，隋遣尚書左僕射高熲出寧州道，內史監虞慶則出原州道，以擊突厥。

translations.literal: 19 On renwu Sui sent Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Jiong out by the Ningzhou route and Palace Supervisor Yu Qingze out by the Yuanzhou route to strike the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: 19 On renwu Sui sent Left Vice Director Gao Jiong by the Ningzhou road and Palace Supervisor Yu Qingze by the Yuanzhou road against the Türks.

sentences.zh: 20九月，癸丑，隋大赦。

translations.literal: 20 In the ninth month, on guichou, Sui proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: 20 In the ninth month, on guichou, Sui proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲戌，隋廢河南道行台省，以秦王俊為秦州總管，隴右諸州盡隸焉。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiaxu, Sui abolished the Henan Circuit Directorate and made Prince Jun of Qin commander of Qinzhou, with all Longyou prefectures placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiaxu, Sui abolished the Henan Circuit Directorate, made Prince Jun of Qin commander of Qinzhou, and placed all Longyou prefectures under his command.

sentences.zh: 21丁酉，立皇弟叔平為湘東王，叔敖為臨賀王，叔宣為陽山王，叔穆為西陽王。

translations.literal: 21 On dingyou the emperor's younger brothers Shuping was made Prince of Xiangdong, Shu'ao Prince of Linhe, Shuxuan Prince of Yangshan, and Shumu Prince of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: 21 On dingyou the emperor enfeoffed his brothers Shuping as Prince of Xiangdong, Shu'ao as Prince of Linhe, Shuxuan as Prince of Yangshan, and Shumu as Prince of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，侍中建昌侯徐陵卒。

translations.literal: On wuxu Attendant-in-Ordinary and Marquis of Jianchang Xu Ling died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Attendant-in-Ordinary Xu Ling, Marquis of Jianchang, died.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，立皇弟叔儉為安南王，叔澄為南郡王，叔興為沅陵王，叔韶為岳山王，叔純為新興王。

translations.literal: On guichou the emperor's younger brothers Shujian was made Prince of Annan, Shucheng Prince of Nanjun, Shuxing Prince of Yuanling, Shushao Prince of Yueshan, and Shuchun Prince of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou the emperor enfeoffed his brothers Shujian as Prince of Annan, Shucheng as Prince of Nanjun, Shuxing as Prince of Yuanling, Shushao as Prince of Yueshan, and Shuchun as Prince of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 22十一月，遣散騎常侍周墳、通直散騎常侍袁彥聘於隋。

translations.literal: 22 In the eleventh month he sent Regular Attendant Zhou Fen and Direct Regular Attendant Yuan Yan on a mission of courtesy to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: 22 In the eleventh month he sent Regular Attendant Zhou Fen and Direct Regular Attendant Yuan Yan on a diplomatic mission to Sui.

sentences.zh: 帝聞隋主狀貌異人，使彥畫像而歸。

translations.literal: The emperor had heard that the Sui ruler's appearance was extraordinary and had Yan paint his portrait to bring back.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Sui emperor's bearing was uncanny, he had Yan paint his portrait and return with it.

sentences.zh: 帝見，大駭曰：「吾不欲見此人。

translations.literal: When the emperor saw it, he cried out in alarm: "I do not wish to see this man.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen emperor looked and cried out in alarm: "I do not want to look upon this man.

sentences.zh: 」亟命屏之。

translations.literal: " He at once ordered it screened away.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately ordered the portrait removed.

sentences.zh: 隋既班律令，蘇威屢欲更易事條，內史令李德林曰：「修律令時，公何不言？

translations.literal: After Sui had promulgated its statutes and ordinances, Su Wei repeatedly wished to change various articles; Secretariat Director Li Delin said: "When the statutes were being revised, why did you not speak?
translations.idiomatic: Once Sui had issued its code, Su Wei often wanted to revise individual articles; Secretariat Director Li Delin said: "When the laws were being drafted, why did you stay silent?

sentences.zh: 今始頒行，且宜專守，自非大為民害，不可數更。

translations.literal: They have only now been issued; for the time being you should hold strictly to them. Unless they greatly harm the people, they must not be changed repeatedly."
translations.idiomatic: They have only just been promulgated; for now hold to them faithfully. Unless a rule gravely injures the people, do not keep altering it."

sentences.zh: 河南道行台兵部尚書楊尚希曰：「竊見當今郡縣，倍多於古。

translations.literal: Henan Circuit Director of War Yang Shangxi said: "I observe that today's commanderies and counties are far more numerous than in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shangxi, Director of War on the Henan Circuit, said: "I see that commanderies and counties today far outnumber those of old.

sentences.zh: 或地無百里，數縣並置；

translations.literal: Some lands are less than a hundred li across, yet several counties are set up side by side;
translations.idiomatic: Some tracts are under a hundred li wide, yet several counties are planted together;

sentences.zh: 或戶不滿千，二郡分領。

translations.literal: some have fewer than a thousand households, yet two prefectures divide rule over them.
translations.idiomatic: some have fewer than a thousand households, yet two prefectures share them.

sentences.zh: 具僚已眾，資費日多；

translations.literal: Full staffs are already numerous and expenses grow daily;
translations.idiomatic: Staffs are already swollen and costs mount daily;

sentences.zh: 吏卒增培，租調歲減；

translations.literal: clerks and soldiers increase in heaps while land tax and corvée levies shrink year by year;
translations.idiomatic: clerks and soldiers multiply while grain levies and corvée shrink each year;

sentences.zh: 民少官多，十羊九牧。

translations.literal: few people, many officials—ten sheep, nine shepherds.
translations.idiomatic: few people and many officials—ten sheep with nine herdsmen.

sentences.zh: 今存要去閒，並小為大，國家則不虧粟帛，選舉則易得賢良。

translations.literal: If we now keep what is essential, remove what is idle, merge small units into large ones, the state will not lose grain and silk, and in selection it will be easier to obtain worthy men."
translations.idiomatic: Keep what matters, cut what is idle, merge small into large, and the state will not lose grain and cloth while appointments will more easily find able men."

sentences.zh: 」蘇威亦請廢郡。

translations.literal: " Su Wei also asked to abolish commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: " Su Wei likewise petitioned to abolish the commandery tier.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 甲午，悉罷諸郡為州。

translations.literal: On jiawu all commanderies were abolished and made into prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu every commandery was abolished and converted into a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 23十二月，乙卯，隋遣兼散騎常侍曹令則、通直散騎常侍魏澹來聘。

translations.literal: 23 In the twelfth month, on yimao, Sui sent Concurrent Regular Attendant Cao Lingze and Direct Regular Attendant Wei Dan on a mission of courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: 23 In the twelfth month, on yimao, Sui sent Concurrent Regular Attendant Cao Lingze and Direct Regular Attendant Wei Dan on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 澹，收之族也。

translations.literal: Dan was of the clan of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dan belonged to the house of Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 24丙辰，司空長沙王叔堅免。

translations.literal: 24 On bingchen Minister of Works and Prince of Changsha Shujian was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: 24 On bingchen Prince of Changsha Shujian was removed as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 叔堅既失恩，心不自安，乃為厭媚，醮日月以求福。

translations.literal: Shujian, having lost favor, was ill at ease in heart; he practiced sorcery and held libations to sun and moon to seek blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of favor, Shujian could not rest easy; he turned to sorcery and offered rites to sun and moon for good fortune.

sentences.zh: 或上書告其事，帝召叔堅，囚於西省，將殺之，令近侍宣敕數之。

translations.literal: Someone memorialized against him; the emperor summoned Shujian, imprisoned him in the Western Office, and was about to kill him, ordering a close attendant to proclaim the charges.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial accused him; the emperor summoned Shujian, held him in the Western Office, and prepared to execute him, sending a close attendant to recite his crimes.

sentences.zh: 叔堅對曰：「臣之本心，非有他故，但欲求親媚耳。

translations.literal: Shujian replied: "Your servant's original intent held no other purpose; I only sought to win affection through charm."
translations.idiomatic: Shujian answered: "My heart held no other aim; I only wished to win your affection by such means."

sentences.zh: 臣既犯天憲，罪當萬死。

translations.literal: I have violated Heaven's law and deserve death ten thousand times over.
translations.idiomatic: I have offended Heaven's statute and deserve ten thousand deaths.

sentences.zh: 臣死之日，必見叔陵，願宣明詔，責之於九泉之下。

translations.literal: On the day I die I am sure to meet Shuling; I beg that Your Majesty proclaim the edict clearly and rebuke him in the realm below."
translations.idiomatic: When I die I shall surely meet Shuling; I beg Your Majesty to make the decree plain and reproach him in the world below."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃赦之，免官而已。

translations.literal: The emperor then pardoned him and merely removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then spared him and only stripped him of rank.

sentences.zh: 25隋以上柱國竇榮定為右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: 25 Sui appointed Pillar of State Dou Rongding Grand General of the Right Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: 25 Sui made Pillar of State Dou Rongding Grand General of the Right Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 榮定妻，隋主姊安成公主也。

translations.literal: Rongding's wife was the Sui ruler's elder sister, Princess Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rongding's wife was the emperor's elder sister, Princess Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 隋主欲以榮定為三公，辭曰：「衛、霍、梁、鄧，若少自貶損，不至覆宗。

translations.literal: The Sui ruler wished to make Rongding one of the Three Excellencies; he declined, saying: "Wei Qing, Huo Qubing, Liang Ji, and Deng Yu—had they humbled themselves a little, they would not have brought their clans to ruin."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to name Rongding one of the Three Excellencies; he refused, saying: "Wei Qing, Huo Qubing, Liang Ji, and Deng Yu—had any of them lowered himself a little, his house would not have been destroyed."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 帝以李穆功大，詔曰：「法備小人，不防君子。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Li Mu's merit was great, issued an edict saying: "Law is complete against petty men and does not guard against gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Mu's service was immense, the emperor proclaimed: "Law restrains the base, not the noble.

sentences.zh: 太師申公，自今雖有罪，但非謀逆，縱有百死，終不推問。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Duke Shen—from this day forward, though he commit crimes, unless it be treason, even if he deserve death a hundred times, in the end he shall not be interrogated."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Duke Shen—from this day, though he sin, unless it be treason, even for a hundred capital crimes he shall never be questioned."

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書牛弘請立明堂，帝以時事草創，不許。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Niu Hong asked to establish the Bright Hall; the emperor, because the times were still in founding turmoil, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Niu Hong petitioned to build the Bright Hall; the emperor, finding the realm still newly founded, refused.

sentences.zh: 帝覽刑部奏，斷獄數猶至萬。

translations.literal: The emperor reviewed the Ministry of Justice's reports; cases adjudicated still reached ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the Ministry of Justice's returns, he found judgments still running to ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 以為律尚嚴密，故人多陷罪。

translations.literal: He thought the statutes were still too severe and dense, and therefore many people fell into crime.
translations.idiomatic: He judged the code still too tight, so that many were trapped by it.

sentences.zh: 又敕蘇威、牛弘等更定新律，除死罪八十一條，流罪一百五十四條，徒杖等千餘條，唯定留五百條，凡十二卷。

translations.literal: He again ordered Su Wei, Niu Hong, and others to revise the new statutes, removing eighty-one articles on capital punishment, one hundred fifty-four on exile, and more than a thousand on penal servitude and beating; only five hundred articles were retained in all, twelve scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Su Wei, Niu Hong, and others to recast the code, striking eighty-one capital articles, one hundred fifty-four on exile, and more than a thousand on servitude and flogging, leaving five hundred articles in twelve scrolls.

sentences.zh: 自是刑網簡要，疏而不失。

translations.literal: From this the penal net was brief and simple, loose yet without loss.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the penal net was concise—broad yet without losing hold.

sentences.zh: 仍置律博士弟子員。

translations.literal: He also established posts for erudites of statutes and student disciples.
translations.idiomatic: He also set up statutory erudites and student posts.

sentences.zh: 隋主以長安倉廩尚虛，是歲，詔西自蒲、陝，東至衛、汴，水次十三州，募丁運米。

translations.literal: The Sui ruler, because Chang'an's granaries were still empty, in this year issued an edict that from Pu and Shan in the west to Wei and Bian in the east, thirteen prefectures along the waterways should conscript laborers to transport grain.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Chang'an's granaries still bare, that year he ordered thirteen riverine prefectures from Pu and Shan in the west to Wei and Bian in the east to levy men to haul grain.

sentences.zh: 又於衛州置黎陽倉，陝州置常平倉，華州置廣通倉，轉相灌輸。

translations.literal: He also established Liyang Granary at Weizhou, Changping Granary at Shanzhou, and Guangtong Granary at Huazhou, to relay supplies in turn.
translations.idiomatic: He built Liyang Granary at Weizhou, Changping at Shanzhou, and Guangtong at Huazhou, to relay grain in succession.

sentences.zh: 漕關東及汾、晉之粟以給長安。

translations.literal: Grain from east of the Pass and from Fen and Jin was transported by water to supply Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Grain from east of the Pass and from Fen and Jin was shipped by water to feed Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 26時刺史多任武將，類不稱職。

translations.literal: 26 At this time many prefects were military men, and as a rule they did not fit their posts.
translations.idiomatic: 26 Many prefects were now soldiers, and most were unfit for civil rule.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史柳彧上表曰：「昔漢光武與二十八將，披荊棘，定天下，及功成之後，無所任職。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Yu submitted a memorial, saying: "Formerly Emperor Guangwu of Han, with his twenty-eight generals, cleared thorns and brambles and settled the realm; when merit was complete, none held further office.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Yu memorialized: "When Emperor Guangwu of Han and his twenty-eight generals cut through hardship and pacified the empire, once the work was done none of them held office.

sentences.zh: 伏見詔書，以上柱國和千子為杞州刺史。

translations.literal: I observe in the edict that Pillar of State He Qianzi was made prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I see an edict making Pillar of State He Qianzi prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 千子前任趙州，百姓歌之曰：『老禾不早殺，余種穢良田。

translations.literal: When Qianzi was earlier at Zhao, the people sang of him: 'The old grain is not cut down early; the leftover seed fouls the good field.'
translations.idiomatic: When Qianzi governed Zhao the people sang: 'The old stalk is not reaped in time; the leftover seed spoils the good field.'

sentences.zh: 』千子，弓馬武用，是其所長；

translations.literal: Qianzi's bow, horse, and martial use are what he excels at;
translations.idiomatic: Qianzi excels at bow, horse, and martial arts;

sentences.zh: 治民蒞職，非其所解。

translations.literal: Governing the people and holding office were not what he understood.
translations.idiomatic: Governing the people and holding civil office were beyond his competence.

sentences.zh: 如謂優老尚年，自可厚賜金帛；

translations.literal: If one means to honor the aged and respect years, he could simply be richly rewarded with gold and silk;
translations.idiomatic: If the aim is to honor his age, let him be rewarded generously with gold and silk;

sentences.zh: 若令刺舉，所損殊大。

translations.literal: but if he is made to investigate and impeach, the harm would be very great.
translations.idiomatic: but to make him a provincial inspector would do great harm.

sentences.zh: 」帝善之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 千子竟免。

translations.literal: Qianzi was spared after all.
translations.idiomatic: He Qianzi was not appointed after all.

sentences.zh: 彧見上勤於聽受，百僚奏請，多有煩碎，上疏諫曰：「臣聞上古聖帝，莫過唐、虞，不為叢脞，是謂欽明。

translations.literal: Yu saw that the emperor was diligent in listening and accepting, while the hundred officials' memorials and requests were often trivial and minute; he submitted a remonstrance saying, "Your servant has heard that among the sage emperors of high antiquity none surpass Yao and Shun, who did not busy themselves with trifles—this is called reverent clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu saw the emperor laboring over every petition while officials flooded him with trivial business; he memorialized: "The sage rulers of antiquity, Yao and Shun above all, did not drown in petty detail—that is true sagely government.

sentences.zh: 舜任五臣，堯咨四岳，垂拱無為，天下以治。

translations.literal: Shun employed five ministers; Yao consulted the Four Peaks; they folded their robes and did nothing, and the realm was governed.
translations.idiomatic: Shun entrusted five ministers; Yao consulted the Four Peaks; they ruled with folded hands, and the realm was well ordered.

sentences.zh: 所謂勞於求賢，逸於任使。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by toiling in seeking the worthy and resting in employing them.
translations.idiomatic: They toiled to find the worthy and rested once they were employed.

sentences.zh: 比見陛下留心治道，無憚疲勞，亦由群官懼罪，不能自決，取判天旨，聞奏過多。

translations.literal: Recently Your Majesty has devoted his mind to the way of governance and feared no fatigue; this is also because the host of officials, fearing guilt, cannot decide for themselves and seek judgment from Heaven's intent—reports to the throne are too many.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now applies himself tirelessly to government, but officials, fearing blame, refuse to decide anything and push every matter to you—hence the flood of memorials.

sentences.zh: 乃至營造細小之事，出給輕微之物，一日之內，酬答百司。

translations.literal: It reaches the point that on matters of petty construction and the issue of trifling goods, within a single day he replies to the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Even minor construction projects and petty supplies draw your reply to a hundred offices in a single day.

sentences.zh: 至乃日旰忘食，夜分未寢，動以文簿憂勞聖躬。

translations.literal: He even forgets food when the sun is low and does not sleep when night is half spent, constantly vexing the sacred person with documents and ledgers.
translations.idiomatic: You work past sunset without eating and past midnight without sleep, wearing yourself down over paperwork.

sentences.zh: 伏願察臣至言，少減煩務，若經國大事，非臣下裁斷者，伏願詳決，自余細務，責成所司；

translations.literal: Your servant wishes you would examine his utmost words and reduce troublesome duties a little; if they are great affairs of state that subordinates cannot judge, your servant wishes you would decide them in detail; as for the rest, the trivial affairs, charge the responsible offices;
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to heed these words and lighten your burden: decide in person only great matters of state that subordinates cannot judge; leave the rest to the offices responsible;

sentences.zh: 則聖體盡無疆之壽，臣下蒙覆育之賜。

translations.literal: then the sacred person will enjoy boundless years of life, and your servants below will receive the gift of sheltering nurture.
translations.idiomatic: then Your Majesty will enjoy long life, and your servants the blessing of your care.

sentences.zh: 」上覽而嘉之，因曰：「柳彧直士，國之寶也！

translations.literal: " The emperor read it and praised it, saying, "Liu Yu is a straight man—a treasure of the state!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor read the memorial with approval and said, "Liu Yu is an upright man—a treasure to the state!

sentences.zh: 彧以近世風俗，每正月十五日，然燈遊戲，奏請禁之，曰：「竊見京邑，爰及外州，每以正月望夜，充街塞陌，聚戲朋游，鳴鼓聒天，燎炬照地，竭貲破產，競此一時。

translations.literal: Yu, because recent custom on the fifteenth day of the first month each year was to light lamps and play games, memorialized asking that it be forbidden, saying, "Your servant has observed that in the capital and extending to the outer provinces, on the full-moon night of the first month the streets and lanes are packed, crowds gather for sport and roaming, drums deafen heaven, torches light the ground, fortunes are exhausted and families ruined—all to compete in this one moment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, deploring the custom of lantern festivals on the fifteenth of the first month, asked that it be banned: "In the capital and in the provinces alike, on the full-moon night of the first month the streets are jammed with revelers, drums deafen the heavens, torches blaze, and families ruin themselves in a single night's frenzy.

sentences.zh: 盡室並孥，無問貴賤，男女混雜，緇素不分。

translations.literal: Whole households go out together, regardless of noble or base; men and women mingle, and black-robed and white-robed are not distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Whole families turn out, high and low alike; men and women mingle without restraint, and laymen and clergy are not kept apart.

sentences.zh: 穢行因此而生，盜賊由斯而起，因循弊風，會無先覺。

translations.literal: Filthy conduct arises from this, and thieves and robbers spring from it; following a corrupt custom, none has yet awakened beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: From this come debauchery and theft; the evil custom persists because no one has yet put a stop to it.

sentences.zh: 無益於化，實損於民。

translations.literal: It benefits transformation not at all and truly harms the people.
translations.idiomatic: It does nothing for moral order and truly harms the people.

sentences.zh: 請頒天下，並即禁斷。

translations.literal: Your servant asks that it be proclaimed throughout the realm and at once forbidden and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that this be forbidden throughout the empire at once.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved his request.
